📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it’s no secret that Taylor Swift has amassed a large group of celebrity friends. Selena Gomez, Ed Sheeran and Sabrina Carpenter are just a few of the major names that make up Swift’s personal orbit. The beloved pop star has spoken quite a bit about friendship over the years and, most recently, she spoke about it in reference to her involvement with the 2026 movie schedule entry Toy Story 5. Swift’s latest sentiments on the subject are particularly poignant given where she reportedly stands with Karlie Kloss and Blake Lively.

For the latest Toy Story film, Swift wrote and recorded an original song, “I Knew It, I Knew You,” and it’s currently nominated for two Grammy Awards. Swift has been making the rounds amid awards season, helping the Pixar team promote the legacy sequel, which seems to be a serious contender for some major awards. During a press conference, Swift discussed (via Hello!) the acclaimed movie’s theme of friendship and stressed the importance of someone looking back on such intimate bonds. She also noted this:.

You may feel, ‘Oh, that friend I had, that was really a special time, and even though I don't know that person anymore, I hope they're doing great,’ or feeling like you could count on your friends to be there when you needed them; feeling like you don't need to have a million of the wrong friends.

The “Delicate” performer’s comments fall directly in line with the narrative of the new Toy Story film, which sees young Bonnie attempting to make genuine friendships. At the same time, cowgirl doll Jessie also reflects fondly on the bond she had with her former owner, Emily. Those plot threads culminated into a truly sentimental third act for the billion-dollar-grossing film. Aside from that, though, Swift’s thoughts are indeed sweet, and they do speak to the nature of how friends come in and out of our lives as time goes on.

Industry observers note that given Swift’s sentiments, it’s honestly hard not to think about her own girl squad and where she stands with certain people. Her relationships with Lively and Kloss have been significant topics of discussion over the past year, and there are a few reasons for that.

We Know Taylor Swift And Travis Kelce Mentioned 'No Gifts' At Their Wedding (But They Did Ask Guests For Something).

The Swift/Kloss friendship began in 2012 after the two publicly showed admiration for each other, and they remained tight until rumors of a falling-out between the two surfaced in 2018., By 2019, it was alleged that Kloss’ continued friendship with former talent manager Scooter Braun (who was in conflict with Swift over her music catalogue) served as a point of contention. While Swift and Kloss wouldn’t be spotted publicly for years after that, the latter surprisingly attended an Eras Tour show. Also, Kloss’ presence at Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding in July 2026 and her subsequent attendance at Chiefs games also seemed to suggest the two were friends again.

Meanwhile, Lively and Swift’s friendship seems to be in a very different place. The pair became friends around 2015 and, for years, they were chummy, even attending Chiefs games together. However, the friendship reportedly soured in early 2025 when Swift was pulled into Lively’s It Ends with Us drama with Justin Baldoni. The rumors of a strained friendship seemed to be confirmed when Lively and husband Ryan Reynolds weren’t invited to Swift’s wedding.

According to recent reports, something that should be made clear in all of this, however, is that Taylor Swift hasn’t publicly addressed the states of her relationships with Blake Lively and Karlie Kloss. With that, the general public can only speculate as to where Swift truly stands with these other stars. Regardless, considering how much emphasis Swift places on the importance of friendship – whether that be related to Toy Story 5 or not – I wouldn’t be surprised if fans were to continue to keep eyes on her friend group.

After GTA 6's original soundtrack, Justice probably won't work on any other video game ever again

  • Sources indicate that from what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that you've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer. Featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and the fantastic King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, it's clear that the duo - and Rockstar - have spared no expense on the production of music for the game.

Sources indicate that from what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City. You ought to enjoy the music while you can, though, because it seems Justice won't be coming back to video games any time soon. If ever.

Via a newly introduced interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project. "When [the offer to work with Rockstar] arrived on the table, we thought 'if there’s one video game we have to do, it's this one.' As soon as we accepted and started working [on the OST], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game.".

Interesting. The duo, from the clip we can see on Rockyrama's posts, don't seem to give more information about this decision - did they have a bad time working with Rockstar? Was it intense? Or is it rather down to the fact that, if you're going to work on a game, you may as well make it what is largely expected to be the biggest game of all time.

Justice, for what it's worth, consider the work they've done on GTA 6 to be "a real album" of music - it's not seen as lesser or different to the band, just because it's being released as part of a video game. "GTA 6 gave us the excuse and direction to do it. The music always had to be listenable on its own, even if each track is tailored for [a specific] scene," the band explains.

The band's album isn't the only music connected to the game, either. There's also a 34-song album launching for the game, composed of original songs from some of the biggest artists in the world. The album features Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson and many more. The full tracklist leaked at the weekend.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 debuts on Thursday, 19th November for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is a game that at times feels almost embarrassingly expensive and extravagant. I cleaned a boat with a pressure washer and watched the suds build up realistically in the concrete below my characterâs flip-flops. I ran through a tram station and spotted over 100 different NPCs milling about, all unique and all moving. Hair gets wet. Sweat builds up on backs. Even for Rockstar, the master of tiny details, GTA 6 is overflowing with examples of what happens when you let a studio work on one game for a decade. Itâs a lot, but it all serves the purpose of creating a virtual world that players can truly get lost in.Â.

Iâve put over 150 hours into GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 Pro, and I expect Iâll spend even more time in this digital recreation of Florida and Miami, as thereâs so much to do and see in Vice City. I doubt most players will see half of it. I bet I wonât ever see it all.Â.

GTA 6 is a massive third-person open-world game, like Rockstarâs previous offerings. It merges the slower pace and slice-of-life mechanics from Red Dead Redemption 2 with the urban sprawl and crime-movie feel of GTA IV and GTA V. Itâs a more grounded journey than its predecessors, one which requires more planning and consideration if you want to survive and succeed as modern-day Bonnie and Clyde, robbing small stores as you work your way up to bigger scores, like banks. Itâs often a tougher game than any past GTA, but in a way that rewards skill and patience. Or bravery, stupidity, and luck.Â.

I have quibbles about some clunky controls and some story pacing problems in the gameâs later chapters, but like crappy cupholders in a million-dollar supercar, they donât really get in the way of what’s here. Instead, they’re minor concerns to point at as I hit the gas and go 200 MPH with the radio blasting.Â.

Industry observers note that the best part of Grand Theft Auto 6 isnât what I expected. It’s not the crime, or the action, or the massive world to explore, though all of those parts are excellent and better than ever. The real standout of GTA 6, the part of the game that kept me hooked and which I wonât forget anytime soon, is its central duo, Jason and Lucia.

Not only do they have very different motivations than past GTA protagonists, wanting to create a better life for themselves and escape their life of crime instead of vying to become crime lords or get revenge, but they are easily Rockstarâs most fully fleshed-out, believable, and relatable characters.

At the start of the game, Jason and Lucia are separated after a short relationship. Lucia tried to rob a payday loan place after breaking up with Jason and, in the process, got arrested. This moment has huge ramifications for both of their lives and ultimately pulls them together early on in GTA 6âs runtime.

Sources indicate that jason, an Army vet, is more reserved than your average GTA protagonist. Heâs a loyal man who’s conflicted about the things he does to get by and try to make things better for himself and Lucia. A lot of people tell Jason heâs a good guy, but heâs never sure if he really is. Meanwhile, Lucia, a petty thief living paycheck to paycheck, knows sheâs flawed and doesnât care nearly as much as Jason about that fact. Sheâs more focused on improving her life by any means and has a bigger goal that drives her to take bigger risks.Â.

In a recent development, together they balance each other out, with Jason often acting as a voice of reason and Lucia pushing him to strive for more. Their dynamic is unlike anything Iâve seen in a Rockstar-developed game, and thanks to some stellar writing and performances, I found myself deeply caring about these two criminals just trying to make it.Â.

According to recent reports, throughout the entire run of GTA 6, Jason and Lucia interact as you would expect two real people who care for each other would. They joke with each other, comment on events happening around them, share secrets, and help each other when they can.Â.

Spending time with them is never annoying. Neither Lucia nor Jason pesters the player when youâre hanging around with them in the open world. Sometimes they might point out that you missed a turn or a possible way to sneak into a gang-infested hideout. This never felt like some annoying video-gamey handholding, just a couple working together.Â.

While Jason and Lucia are both skilled at stealing cars, shooting guns, and running around causing chaos, they arenât always treated as equals in the world. While playing as Lucia, I was hit on by random assholes and catcalled by men on the street. It wasnât constant, but it happened enough that it was impossible to ignore. Some characters will also doubt Luciaâs abilities, but never question Jasonâs skills as a murderous criminal. It adds an intriguing wrinkle to playing as either character. Lucia feels like she has to work harder to prove herself among her criminal peers. Jason often has her back in these scenarios, but lets her hold her own, and she does so with sharp words and strong punches.Â.

Even outside of when they directly speak to each other to tell stories or give feedback, the other’s presence is always felt, sometimes in small gestures, like one holding the door for the other as they enter a building. And sometimes, depending on how you handle their relationship, through more intimate moments that either Jason or Lucia, regardless of whether the player is controlling them, can initiate when theyâre feeling ready to fool around.Â.

It has been revealed that one time while I was playing as Jason, after spending all day and most of the night with Lucia, we came home, and I couldnât even get through the door before both of them were on top of each other. If you were wondering: Jason and Lucia fuck a lot in this game, assuming you play them as a couple, which I did.Â.

Recent findings suggest that it didnât take long for me to fall in love with Jason and Lucia. And I spent the entire game rooting for them, even as their situation became more dangerous and desperate, largely due to factors outside of their control.Â.

While Jason and Luciaâs relationship, be it platonic or romantic depending on your choices, never loses steam or feels like it stops evolving, GTA 6âs main overarching narrative of criminal conspiracy and mayhem does start to falter in the back half.

In a later chapter of the story, the momentum that had carried everything forward up until that point fades. It feels like GTA 6âs story begins spinning its wheels at this point. By the end, the narrative picks back up, and the stakes grow even larger as Jason and Lucia rely on themselves to take on the world. But even when the story started to lose steam, and I felt myself wondering how many more missions Iâd have to do before something substantial happened, Jason and Lucia were there to keep me going. Lucia doing an impersonation of Jasonâs deep voice always made me chuckle, as did any time Jason gave her crap about her bad driving after I crashed another car.Â.

Just know there are multiple endings, and after seeing two of them in my time with the game, I can confirm that how you play and what choices you make can have a huge impact on how things turn out. Happy endings areâ¦not common in this line of work, but not impossible.Â.

Even if the rest of GTA 6 didnât work, Jason, Lucia, and their relationship would still carry it across the finish line. Thankfully, the rest of Grand Theft Auto 6 is very good, too.Â.

The second-best part of GTA 6, behind our Bonnie and Clyde duo, is the world of Leonida, the state that Vice City is located in. It is the most detailed, gorgeous, and alive open world Iâve ever experienced in a video game.Â.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 starts off in the southern part of the map, far away from the skyscrapers and glitz of Vice City. You can almost see it in the distance from the small coastal town where GTA 6 begins. Itâs the kind of scale Iâve not really felt before in an open-world game. And all that spaceâ¦it ainât empty.Â.

Industry observers note that it feels like every inch of GTA 6 is filled with life. With movement. Withâ¦something. Even areas like the huge swamp, which at first glance might seem empty, reveal themselves to be filled with detail and specificity. That swamp, for instance, is teeming with creatures, big and small. The wind rustles the leaves of every tree and plant around. Planes fly overhead at different altitudes. I ran deeper in and stumbled upon a giant snake with a dead body in its mouth. Later, I found a crashed plane smuggling drugs. In the distance, I spotted dark clouds forming and bursts of lightning. Rain was coming. And later, I watched a lightning bolt crash into the woods and start a small fire.Â.

It has been revealed that all this happened in the span of an hour in one relatively small section of the swamp, itself a small portion of the larger world. Itâs at times overwhelming. Driving through the city, which I didnât reach until nearly a dozen hours into the game, I felt guilty about all the life and detail I was speeding by at 100 MPH.Â.

Recent findings suggest that I was also much more focused on the road than in past GTA games. The streets in GTA 6 arenât as wide as those in GTA V, and there are far more cars on the road. Crashing into these other drivers can swiftly damage your vehicle, making it harder to steer or accelerate. But I didnât find any of this annoying. Instead, it made it satisfying to weave through traffic to escape police. The act of just driving a car is so much more exciting than it’s ever been in the franchise. It felt like a real skill Iâd developed after a few hours and one which I always enjoyed using, making long road trips across the map feel less like a chore and more like an opportunity to explore more of the game.Â.

It has been revealed that all of these changes to driving and the roads in GTA 6 also forced me to sometimes slow down or stop, giving me more time to take in all the atmosphere and detail packed into the game.Â And I do recommend slowing down whenever possible and just soaking in Vice City and Leonida. GTA 6 is a game that truly rewards exploration and poking around. Even 150 hours in, Iâm still encountering new random events, side characters, and more.

One day in Vice City, as I was walking down the street, I entered a small convenience store to buy some food and boost my health stat. But inside, I found a criminal behind the cash register and a dead body on the floor near them. I held the left trigger to lock onto the robber, a young woman, and questioned her about what was happening. She mentioned to mind my own business and leave. I taunted her next. This was a mistake. The young woman robbing the small store was armed with a gun and pointed it at me. I swiftly drew my own pistol, and we started shooting. A second later, she was dead. I grabbed the cashâI mean, I couldnât just leave it there on the groundâand ran out the back where I found the robberâs car. In the trunk were drugs and ammo. Before I could look around more, I heard sirens. The cops were coming. I quickly hopped a fence and ran by some people who werenât happy that I was running through their backyard.Â.

Sources indicate that just another day in Leonida. Iâve truly never experienced an open world like this before, and every time I think Iâve seen it all or canât be more impressed by it than I already am, Iâm promptly proven wrong.Â.

According to recent reports, one night, I climbed the gameâs tallest mountain, and when I reached the top, it was nighttime. Vice City and its sprawl were laid out in front of me, thousands of twinkling lights and bright dots floating in the darkness miles and miles away. Lucia took it in and exclaimed to Jason that it was gorgeous. He agreed. So did I.Â.

It has been revealed that but it ainât just a big pretty world with lots of moving parts. Itâs also Rockstarâs attempt to simulate as much of life in Leonida as possible. Youâll find over 600 stores to shop at, gyms to work out in, gun ranges to visit, golf courses to play on, zoos to explore, gas stations to rob, bars to chill in, animals to hunt, mod shops to improve cars at, and even working buses and trains with actual schedules and passengers.Â.

You can, and I did, just live out a normal day in the life of Jason and Lucia, freely swapping between them to see what the other was up to at any time.Â.

During one session as Jason, I hit the gym early in the morning, then hopped in my off-road car and headed north to do some hunting. When I wanted to shake things up, I swapped over to Lucia, and a few seconds later I was playing as her. She was chilling on a beach, and a friend of hersâthey each have their own social livesâtexted, checking in on me. I replied and then got hit on by a random asshole. So I taunted him until he called me a bitch and left. A moment later I swapped back to Jason, and he was at a nearby gas station with his gun out. I took the hint and hunted a different kind of animal, and came away $450 richer. Other times Iâd switch to find them watching TV, chatting up a random NPC, or driving around the city.Â.

The incredibly realistic graphics and the focus on simulating not just the fact that your partnerâs life continues when you arenât near them, but that they exist in an entire living world, one where you can gain weight, get tired, and ride the bus, do at times clash with the parts of the game where Rockstar clearly didnât want to annoy people with the sorts of inconveniences that can emerge out of realism.Â.

It has been revealed that for example, every store in the game is open 24 hours a day. This means you can walk into a barber shop at 3 am and get a haircut. To the gameâs credit, the shop was empty besides the employees at that time, something I found true in other stores and locations at odd hours. But these bits of video gameâness stood out all the more because the world was otherwise so lifelike.

All this simulation, fancy visuals, and scale does have a cost. The game runs at 30FPS, even on PS5 Pro. And in some areas of the map, like on the packed streets of Vice City, I noticed framerate drops. I also spotted slowdown during large firefights with police. It never became unplayable, but it does make me curious to see how this game will look on a powerful PC.Â.

If youâve reached this point and are starting to wonder if this is still a GTA game, donât worry; thereâs plenty of shooting, robbing, car theft, murder, and action to be had. But this time around, crime isnât as easy as it has been in the past, which makes it so much more rewarding and fun.Â.

Police in GTA 6 are not to be underestimated. They can quickly overwhelm Lucia and Jason and will share notable details about the couple with each other on the radio, making it harder to evade officers looking for you. It pays to keep a change of clothing in your trunk and store large weapons in there too, unless you want every cop in the area to come calling after people spot an armed person matching a suspected robberâs description.Â.

Even hitting a small gas station is thrilling because of how much smarter police are and how much more challenging GTA 6 can be.

Recent findings suggest that you can walk into a store, pull out a gun, kill the clerk, take his money, and run. But the surveillance camera will record you, people in the area will report your location, and cops will be after you quicker due to the murder and gunfire.Â.

Recent findings suggest that instead, you should sneak in through the back, put on a mask, destroy any camera recordings, disable the alarm, crack open the safe, and then head out front to force the clerk to hand over the cash. Then bail, leaving him alive, and enter your car, which you smartly parked further away from the scene. Once you reach a safe spot, you can change your clothes if you have any heat, and then drive by the cops rushing to the scene without any of them suspecting a thing.Â.

Pulling off perfect crimes like that, even on a small scale, is so rewarding.Â.

Even the simple act of stealing a car in GTA 6 is more engaging and fun than it’s ever been in past games. Some cars are easy to just pop the lock on, hop in, and hotwire. But other cars demand you use a slim jim to shimmy open the lock via a simple, quick mini-game. And still other, fancier cars require Jason and Lucia to use a key cloner to gain access, which is also pulled off via a mini-game. Those cars canât even be hotwired, meaning for a large chunk of the game you have to avoid the coolest cars in Vice City and settle for rust buckets and unlocked sedans. And even some of those cars have trackers that make it easier for police to find you later, and harder to modify and sell them to shops around the city.Â.

But like the slimmer roadways and more punishing crashes, this change to the GTA formula didnât frustrate me. On the contrary, I found it so much more exciting to steal cars in GTA 6. I became skilled at spotting cars that would likely be easier to steal than others without needing to use the car-scanning app included on your in-game phone. (Thereâs also an Instagram-like social media app on there, and you can text and call other characters, including your partner.)Â.

And if you just canât help yourself, well, you can always steal any car driving around the map by yanking its driver out if you really want that badass Banshee. Jason and Lucia can also drive boats, planes, helicopters, dirt bikes, semi-trucks, airboats, buses, bulldozers, jet skis, andâif youâre brave enough to enter the gameâs military baseâeven a jet or tank. Good luck with that.Â.

In a recent development, "Welcome to Vice City. Enjoy spending your next few years exploring every inch of this place!".

Third-person open-world action game with two playable characters and some RPG-like systems, cover-based shooting, and lots of customization options.

Jason and Lucia, the open world, challenging police, skillful driving, mission variety, multiple endings, and the music.

Some clunky controls, performance complications in big fights, and a back half that loses some narrative oomph.

PS5 / PS5 Pro (Played), Xbox Series X/S.

152 hours. Finished main story campaign, saw two different endings, tried out most side activities, completed most side missions, and explored nearly the entire map.

Gunplay, like other parts of the GTA formula, is also more challenging, but better, than ever in GTA 6. Thatâs largely because Rockstar has moved away from the easy auto-aim nonsense of GTA V. Now, combat plays out more like it did in Max Payne 3, with a focus on manual aiming and landing headshots or, if you want to avoid killing people and being labeled a psycho by the in-game criminal profile system, shooting people in the kneecaps. (That profile system can change how characters react and how aggressive police will be when chasing you down.)Â.

Recent findings suggest that guns also feel louder and more powerful. When a robbery goes wrong and bullets start flying, it’s scary and tense, and I always wanted to get out of there as soon as possible. You canât take too much damage before it becomes a problem, so shootouts are risky, but not impossible, to survive. Sometimes, Iâd just wing a cop or gang member in the arm, and theyâd realistically fall back, giving me enough time to slip away before they got back up and started shooting again.Â.

Alongside all these moving parts and systems, a classic Rockstar problem is back in GTA 6: clunky controls.Â.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes Iâd want to loot a body, but instead Jason would try to enter a nearby car. Other times Iâd want to reload my weapon, but Iâd kick someone instead. Getting objects out of trunks can be a real pain in the ass as context-sensitive button prompts appear and disappear based on where your character is looking.

Sources indicate that I also occasionally found the controls a bit hard to keep straight. Every button on the gamepad does something; oftentimes, multiple actions are mapped to one button or a submenu. I still sometimes forget which d-pad button to hold to swap between Lucia and Jason during the heat of combat.Â.

Still, anytime I had issues with the story or some clunky controls, Iâd turn a corner and discover a whole new section of this incredibly detailed world, promptly forgetting about those minor issues. As I mentioned, crappy cup holders donât make a Bugatti any less fun to drive or impressive to sit in. And like those hyper-expensive and perfectly tuned supercars, GTA 6 feels like it was crafted by masters who’ve been making these kinds of open-world games for a long time and are better at it than any other studio by a very wide margin.Â.

Adding to the feeling that Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterclass in open-world game design are the missions. Yes, there are still the classic GTA missions that have you driving somewhere, shooting or stealing stuff, and then driving back to wrap it up. But so many missions in GTA 6 are very different from that usual formula.

A very early mission doesnât even involve guns or crime. Instead, Jason and his buddy Cal just clean up the living room, move a TV, get high, drink beer, and play video games together. We learn a lot about these two and how they care for each other in that moment, and nary a gun was fired or a murder committed.Â.

But there are still plenty of big action-packed missions, and these, too, offer up experiences that arenât the usual GTA fare. A later mission involving a heist that spins out of control had my heart racing as the tension ramped up, and when all hell broke loose, GTA 6âs incredible world and improved combat were on full display.Â.

According to recent reports, another mission involved a massive shootout that started on the street and worked its way through a building and onto a highway. During that whole fight, I was able to find my own way up, and when the game asked me to escape, I was free to do so in any car I wanted.Â.

Industry observers note that thereâs a lot more flexibility in GTA 6âs missions, too. At one point, I was told to chase down a drug runner in a boat. The game asked me to hop on a dirt bike and follow it via a service road. Instead, I hopped into a small speedboat and the game justâ¦ rolled on, even commenting on my change of aims and changing up the objective on the fly. The person I was chasing even seemed to have different voice lines based on my choice.Â.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is constantly reacting to your choices and actions, both in missions and when just out in the open world. It makes everything you do feel more meaningful and crucial, and it makes GTA 6 feel less restrictive than GTA IV and GTA V.Â.

I also appreciated how experimental and creative GTA 6 can be in some of its missions. During one mission, Jason gets drugged and has to fight off tons of armed thugs. But as you run around and shoot, the world and the lights in it pulse with the music. Another mission involves Jason and Lucia robbing a bunch of tiny stores, and this is presented as a playable montage that hops from moment to moment seamlessly as a classic rock song that Rockstarâs embargo forbids me from naming plays in the background.Â.

Industry observers note that the licensed soundtrack is incredible, with a massive list of music across the gameâs various radio stations. And this time around, you can also listen to multiple in-game podcasts, either in your car or on foot via headphones. One is a true-crime podcast hosted by two terrible people that includes an episode dedicated to the serial killer side character in GTA IV.Â.

Sources indicate that just like in past GTA games, thereâs a ton of content to watch on the TV, too, including multiple episodes of animated TV demonstrates parodying American culture, politics, and police. Thereâs also a game show about people identifying men by looking at just their penises. Some of these shows advertise in the world or on social media, too. And characters will talk about shows and other parts of the world and post about them as the game goes on. Itâs just one more thing that makes the world of Vice City feel less like a static playground and more like a real place that reacts to my actions and crimes.

During one random event, I encountered a polar bear being transported to a zoo. I helped some protestors stop the truck, and the bear escaped, killing a few people and then running off in the city. Later, I saw a news article and a social media post about the bear. Another time I saw a viral clip of a stuntman doing a backflip at a football game and ripping open his suit to reveal his penis. Later on, I met that guy selling a cryptocoin and helped him out before he screwed me and some investors over, leading to news stories and social media posts from the tech firm and its angry customers. And then a radio broadcast summed all this up via a short news piece while I was driving around later. This kind of stuff happens all the time in GTA 6, and it makes the whole world feel so alive and reactive.Â.

This is the kind of stuff that elevates Rockstarâs open world above so many others. Sure, others might look good and feature fun missions. But Rockstarâs games are still the best at playing with the player and reacting to them. And GTA 6 takes this to a whole different level.

I also must shout out GTA 6âs original score, composed by Justice. Their soundtrack is a wild and wonderful mix of electronic dance, â80s funk, and rock guitars that permeates the game and adds so much to it. Strange moments are made weirder by their music. Silly moments are made even sillier and heartbreaking moments more painful.Â Iâll be jamming out to the gameâs score for weeks, I suspect. Even if you donât end up liking GTA 6 or even playing it, Justiceâs soundtrack is worth checking out.Â.

A complete review of Grand Theft Auto 6 feels both impossible and in some ways unnecessary. For folks who see reviews as simply text that tells them if a game is worth buying or not, well, this is a game that doesnât need any help convincing people to buy it. And a game of this scale is hard to distill and evaluate, even with thousands of words. I sit here and feel like Iâve left out so much of what GTA 6 is.Â.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 is not the kind of game we get very often. Itâs a massive experience that is filled with more content and more ideas than some entire game franchises.Â.

I had high expectations for Grand Theft Auto 6. This much time and money being poured into one video game leads to a lot of hype. Yet GTA 6 surprised me by not just meeting those expectations, but often exceeding them.Â.

Jason and Lucia feel like a real couple and I loved rooting for them as they tried to escape the shitty hand they’d been dealt. The world is not just massive but also reactive, and feels the closest a video game has ever gotten to truly recreating all the vibes, life, and details youâd expect from a real place. The action is better than ever, but GTA 6âs quiet moments are really where the game leapfrogs over anything seen in a past GTA entry. And it all comes together to deliver something that truly makes the long wait feel both worth it and absolutely necessary.Â.

There were nights when Iâd stay up far too late playing this game, not because I was crunching to finish it before the review embargo, but because I just didnât want to put the controller down.Â.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is a truly remarkable game. A masterpiece of open-world design that brings forward the best parts of all of Rockstarâs past games into one billion-dollar adventure that is unlike anything Iâve played before. Itâs a game Iâll be playing for years, and I canât wait to talk about it with others.Â.

#28139. 100 hours with GTA 6: A sprawling adventure that will be so much better on PC

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2648 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pcgamer ↗ Open Full Page

100 hours with GTA 6: A sprawling adventure that will be so much better on PC

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2648 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 is not on PC so I can't review it.
  • So this isn't a review, but I can give a verdict of sorts:.
  • It has been revealed that it's (mostly) great.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 is not on PC so I can't review it. But somehow I, a member of PC Gamer, got access to GTA 6 before it released. For the past two weeks I've secretly sunk approximately 100 hours in it (on something called a PlayStation 5) and now, finally, I can talk about it. What a relief.

So this isn't a review, but I can give a verdict of sorts:.

It has been revealed that it's (mostly) great. But it will be (mostly) so much greater when it comes to PC.

I guess I shouldn't be surprised by just how massive and detailed the world is. It's Rockstar: huge open worlds is what they do, and they've had a decade to do it. But I was stunned when I started playing, and a hundred hours later, I'm honestly still pretty stunned. Rockstar stated GTA 6's map is twice as big as GTA 5's map, but it feels twice as big as "twice as big" should feel. It's enormous.

It has been revealed that I'm constantly impressed by the macro and micro of it all. I can step back and take in the sheer size and scale of Leonida: the archipelago representing the Florida keys to the south, the vast wetlands standing in for the Everglades, the dense neighborhoods and shining skyscrapers of Vice City, the miles of beaches and forests and industrial areas and state parks. And I can zoom in and admire the tiny details: the carefully placed clutter and photos and belongings in a stranger's apartment, the accurate mating rituals of two great blue herons in the wild, or the font choice on a printout pinned to the wall of an office cubicle instructing employees on breakroom etiquette.

I've lost hours doing nothing but wandering around the world.

I've lost hours doing nothing but wandering around the world, picking a point in the distance that looked interesting and getting distracted by a dozen other things along the way. Exploration is always rewarding: Sometimes, because I find one of hundreds of collectibles hidden throughout the map, but usually because I happen upon an interesting landmark, spot an animal I haven't seen before, stumble into a mysterious scene or sight (I have found many yet haven't unraveled any of them yet), or have a chance encounter with the seemingly inexhaustible supply of "Florida Man"-style weirdos that populate Leonida.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It has been revealed that my only problem with the world is that present day Miami doesn't hold a lot of interest for me, pop-culture-wise. Upcoming York and Los Angeles are fascinating in any era, and I loved the neon-soaked '80s Vice City from Rockstar's game. But GTA 6's Vice City doesn't quite stand up against Liberty City or Los Santos. I'm not saying it's a bad place to spend time: it's an incredible facsimile of the real Miami, with an intense amount of detail and attention paid to the diversity of the city, like its recreation of Little Havana (called Little Cuba here). But it doesn't grab me the way the cities in the last two GTA games did.

It's stressful being in a newly introduced relationship. What if my partner texts me and I don't respond right away? Am I giving them enough attention, or too much attention? If they want to hang out, can I say no if I'm busy doing something else? It's been quite a while since I dated IRL, but the early hours of getting to know Jason and Lucia gave me those early relationship jitters I remember so well.

There are lots of systems in GTA 6 for keeping Jason and Lucia's partnership strong: talking to each other, showing affection, doing activities together, and even committing crimes together will improve their bond. That makes it a little tense when one character wants to do something and you (as the other character) don't.

According to recent reports, one day as I was playing as Jason, Lucia texted me because she wanted to talk about our financial future. But I was on a speedboat halfway across the map and I had just spotted what I suspect was one of Florida's many cryptids (which, after 100 hours, I still cannot confirm is actually in the game or not). Was I really supposed to drop everything I was doing?

In a recent development, I dropped everything I was doing. Instead of becoming a renowned cryptid investigator, Lucia and I went to the bank to set up a savings account. Was I happy about it? Hell no. I was annoyed. But that felt real to me—not the cryptid part, but the idea of being responsible to your partner. While playing them, both individually and together, I wanted to be a good partner, and sometimes that meant glumly turning around my stolen speedboat and having a frank talk about money. It's pretty cool that a game about robbing banks and blowing up police helicopters could make me want to be a good boyfriend.

The two of them are a satisfying couple to play in other respects, too. When knocking over a jewelry store or check-cashing place (cute date idea), your partner can perform crowd control, keeping security guards and employees docile, while you smash open display cases, empty cash drawers, and crack the safe in the back room. During story missions, the duo is often split up and you bounce between their perspectives, with Jason shooting his way through a crowd of goons in an office tower to Lucia fighting hand-to-hand several floors above.

I had a really wonderful two weeks of ignoring my real life partner while spending quality time with these two.

According to recent reports, but the best moments as a duo are when you're coming up with your own ways to play them as a couple. After trying to rip off narcotics from a gang stronghold, I got into a heavy gunfight in a narrow alleyway, and with Lucia on one side and Jason on the other, I was able to fight my way out. As Lucia I could cover Jason as he advanced, and as Jason I could get better angles on the thugs trying to bring Lucia down. It was fluid, fun, and not part of any main mission, just an organic bit of co-op play with me swapping between them as needed. This was the sort of thing that GTA 5 could only pull off in heavily-scripted story missions with its three characters, but here you really are a dynamic duo.

Industry observers note that even more fun? Just hanging out together as a couple. You can take them both to a store to shop for clothes, then compliment each other on their new looks. Or go on a date and play minigolf while gently trash-talking each other. (Tall Jason to short Lucia: "So, is this, like, regular-sized golf to you?") Hit the night clubs and do some dancing. Buy two ice cream cones, hand one to your partner, and enjoy them together. Even just lying in bed, side-by-side, and scrolling your phones is a warm and fuzzy activity amidst all the crime and bloodshed. It's good stuff. I had a really wonderful two weeks of ignoring my real life partner while spending quality time with these two.

It has been revealed that jason and Lucia are a good match for the more deliberate gameplay of GTA 6. Taking a page from Red Dead Redemption 2, your car is basically now your horse: not just a ride, but a gun locker. No longer can you keep a full arsenal in your weapon wheel or unholster a grenade launcher from your back pocket.

It has been revealed that the pair can conceal two handguns in their pants, but "long" guns like shotties and rifles are visible on your back or in your hands. This matters: Even the locals of the gun-friendly Leonida will notice and sometimes panic at the sight of a heavily armed maniac, drawing outright alarm from security guards and cops.

Sources indicate that so you'll have to stash those significant guns in your car until you need them, along with a few changes of clothes because witnesses to your crimes will tell the cops what you're wearing. This makes even a quick, mindless smash-and-grab feel like a mission with phases and choices: scope it out, strategy your moves and escape route, grab your gear, and then afterwards, stow your guns and change clothes once the cops are out of sight. When things go sideways, it can be a lot of fun to scramble your way out of the heat: dumping your big guns in an alleyway and running into a clothing shop to buy some upcoming duds, a hat, and sunglasses, so you don't match the description the cops are looking for.

It has been revealed that and while you can't play entirely non-lethally, you can at least play less-lethally. Using your focus meter (bullet time) will highlight your enemies' elbows, knees, hands, shoulders, and other non-fatal places to deposit a bullet, so you can incapacitate them instead of just headshotting them if that's how you want to roll. I did a lot of that in my playthrough, partly to keep Jason and Lucia feeling less like murdering psychopaths so that I could continue to like them as characters, but also because it added an extra challenge: aiming carefully at joints instead of just popping lead in every dome I see.

Recent findings suggest that playing less lethally is another way GTA 6 makes the near-constant violence a bit less mindless, though trust me, my body count was still pretty high by the end of the main story. It's hard to non-lethally shoot down a helicopter with a grenade launcher from the back of a speedboat.

I don't love everything about GTA 6. The big action setpieces, while technically impressive, usually wind up feeling pretty samey: pull a big score, everything goes wrong, 100 guys show up, shoot all of them in the knees, then drive away, 100 cars show up, shoot all of them them in the tires (tires are a car's knees), escape. Rockstar missions are still Rockstar missions.

As with RDR2, these moments of front-page bombast contradict the fantasy of small-time outlaws struggling to get ahead, and GTA 6 goes full ridiculous with Fast and Furious-style mayhem. I'm not saying those sequences aren't entertaining, they just clash with the story of a couple of star-crossed crooks trying to save up enough money to get out of the game. And after you've shot your hundredth kneecap of the night, it gets a bit tiresome.

I don't love everything about GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that as for the story and characters? It's Rockstar, so some of it is genuinely good but a lot of it is exaggerated bluster. Lucia has some interactions with a family member that feel pretty real and there's a duo of rappers who are fun to spend time with, but I found the majority of the supporting characters either too grating or one-dimensional to care much about. Luckily, the writing and performances of Jason and Lucia make up for that. I enjoyed spending time with them. They had some raw moments that landed well. I felt feelings. I came to care about this couple.

If this is sounding too grown up, don't worry. There's a subplot about furries. A naked guy got into my car and took a sex toy out of his butt. There's a mission where you have to handle multiple dildos. The rideshare app's logo looks like a penis. All the actual penises also look like a penis, too. Rockstar is still Rockstar.

Now that I'm done with the main story, the real game can begin: just having fun in that substantial, beautiful sandbox. And I've got lots left to do: while I mentioned minigolf, there are actual, entire golf courses, too (this is Florida, remember).

I've done a bit of scuba diving for treasure but still have dozens of shipwrecks to discover. I don't find hunting much fun—hitscan sniper rifles aren't satisfying to use—but I sure like spotting newly introduced animals to check off my list, and there are over 200 of them to find. I've only caught one fish. I haven't done any drone races or stunt flying or base jumping or been to a shooting range. There are several in-game videogames I still have to play and a bunch of in-game TV shows to check out. I've somehow hardly gotten anything done in the two weeks I've been playing.

And this is deeply embarrassing, but I barely own any cars! I'm still mainly driving the muscle car I got very early in the game. It's not that there's not a lot to choose from—there are hundreds of autos to theft—it's that the handling and acceleration and physics of every car is different. That's great, obviously, but I promptly got used to driving a few cars and didn't want to have to learn the quirks of more vehicles while fleeing from the cops. Now that the story is behind me, though, it's finally time to start collecting.

I'm still trying to decide where I'd place GTA 6 among Rockstar's other games. RDR2 remains my favorite, followed by Red Dead Redemption, but do I like GTA 6 more than GTA 5? Ultimately, yeah, I just decided while writing this: I do. I like Jason and Lucia more than the three crooks from GTA 5, and maybe even more than I liked Niko Bellic in GTA 4. It's not entirely down to their personalities and performances, but also the systems Rockstar created to let me play as a couple, that make me feel like I had a co-op partner along for the ride.

I'm still trying to decide where I'd place GTA 6 among Rockstar's other games.

In a game like Skyrim where I can have followers, I almost always play solo. But in GTA 6, I found myself calling my partner to meet up almost every time I went out exploring. The game is better when they're together.

Sources indicate that I wish we had some idea of when GTA 6 was coming to PC because after playing almost 100 hours on PS5, I'm desperate to get it on my desktop. I can't wait to see what modders can do with this thing (especially when they fix the weird cheat restrictions). As a PC gamer, I'm dying to aim at people's knees with my mouse instead of a thumbstick. And I'm especially curious to see what Rockstar has planned for an online mode (which they have mentioned nothing about), and how FiveM, which Rockstar now owns, will tie into it. That substantial, beautiful world will only be better on PC where it belongs.

Upgrade 18/11: Crystal Dynamics have provided the following statement to RPS, confirming it cut eight staff members:.

The original article continues below.

Sources indicate that as initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a fresh set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is currently known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.

This now marks the studio's fifth round of layoffs since Embracer acquired it in 2022, following cuts in March 2025, August 2025, November 2025, and March this year. This is a drastic amount even considering the current state of the industry, with layoffs seemingly happening several times a week, but unfortunately, this is par for the course for Embracer. Even still, it makes one wonder just how many staff are left at Crystal Dynamics by now. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and Tomb Raider: Catalyst are still in production, so you'd hope that the studio won't be shuttered entirely.

According to Legacy of Atlantis' Steam page, generative AI has been used in the development of Legacy of Atlantis "to support some early exploration and temporary development content. Any AI-assisted assets were either replaced or refined by humans in order to maintain the creative and artistic vision of the development team." I would hope that this isn't a case of Embracer cutting staff in the misguided hope that they can just be replaced with the use of genAI, but who can say. Solidarity to those affected, who I hope can find new work soon.

Latest Update: "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat" - Square Enix tempts Final Fantasy 14 players back with free game-time to fill void before new expansion

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (578 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February.
  • This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies.
  • Industry observers note that in addition, there's an alluring character skip available too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February. So, in order to keep the game populated for the next few months, Square Enix is running a special promotion in hopes of tempting players back in.

This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies. Lapsed players who haven't logged in for over six months are to be given 30 days of free game time to hop back in and catch up with the main story quest ahead of Evercold's release.

Industry observers note that in addition, there's an alluring character skip available too. If your FF14 character is at least level 90 on one class - the current level-cap is 100 - you can skip all the way to the final part of the latest Dawntrail expansion. You still need to grind to level 100 in preparation for Evercold, but the aforementioned free month of game time should provide plenty of time to do so.

In a producer letter written to accompany this promotion, Naoki Yoshida provided insight into why this was being implemented, stating that retaining players in an MMO like FF14 was of the "utmost importance".

Recent findings suggest that "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat", Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such challenges, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

Sources indicate that "For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn introduced, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today.".

It has been revealed that yoshida went on to explain that promotions such as this are meant as a "tiny nudge". He notes that those who have retained subscriptions continuously remain "the most important" players in the development team's eyes, and acknowledges that the process of catching up in an MMO can seem "daunting" for many.

It has been revealed that this problem of player retention is nothing newly introduced for MMOs, especially in the tricky time between the end of a current expansion and the beginning of a new one. MMO popularity often waxes and wanes, with a new expansion acting as an exciting call to action, with the months leading up to it often serving as a natural break-point for many. Still, monthly subs pay the bills, so keeping folks around even during these quiet months is important.

Industry observers note that final Fantasy 14: Evercold is looking like an especially exciting expansion. On top of the upcoming story and two classes being added, the game is getting an overhaul to combat, with both classic Reborn and Evolved action modes, as well as a new raid difficulty meant to bridge the gap between normal and savage tiers.

Sources indicate that the game has certainly come a long way since its initial release back in 2010. Dawntrail proved divisive among fans too, though with Evercold there's a lot of hope that a new overarching storyline can bring the steal back the hearts of players old and new.

  • It has been revealed that "The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," mentioned Mitsuda.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death. The mangaka, whose art and distinct style were foundational to Chrono Trigger and Chrono Cross - and are still used in Dragon Quest to this day - died in 2024 at the age of 68.

Industry observers note that today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something new. This was all triggered by the announcement of Dragon Quest RPG: The Island of the Demon Tree and the Guided Island, an iOS and Android game that uses art that is very reminiscent of Toriyama's.

It has been revealed that "The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," mentioned Mitsuda. "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly new no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end for now, and [Dragon Quest creator, Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG. (There have been many remakes already.)".

Horii himself seems undeterred: with the new mobile game's announcement last week, he noted that the goal of his new project is to "capture that unmistakable Dragon Quest feeling" that comes with "exploring towns, meeting new allies, gearing up and steadily growing stronger". As Mitsuda calls for the series to retire, and for something new to take its place, Horii is keen to bring "the same classic adventure" to your smartphone.

"What's vital is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future," concluded Mitsuda. "But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people.".

It's unlikely Square Enix is going to want to drop the series, of course: the Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake exceeded Square Enix's (in)famously lofty expectations, and as the organization aggressively pursues its multiplatform strategy, it's hard to imagine a world in which it's going to want to move away from a series that routinely pulls in millions of sales.

Tech Report: Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony.
  • As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.
  • Industry observers note that the lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the tech giant of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

Industry observers note that the lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

It's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

It has been revealed that in a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

As if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

In a recent development, every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another big game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

Breaking: GTA 6 Won’t Get A 60 FPS Mode, Even On PS5 Pro, Because It’s ‘Not Powerful Enough’

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Kotaku

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Earlier this month, Rockstar Games confirmed Grand Theft Auto 6 targets 30 FPS on all platforms, even PlayStation 5 Pro.
  • Industry observers note that when Rockstar revealed that GTA 6 would target 30 FPS on PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S, some players didn’t take it well.
  • However, Rockstar has confirmed with Kotaku that this isn’t going to happen, even on PS5 Pro.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

30 FPSGrand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

Earlier this month, Rockstar Games confirmed Grand Theft Auto 6 targets 30 FPS on all platforms, even PlayStation 5 Pro. Before that news was revealed, I asked Rockstar if GTA 6 could receive a 60 FPS or even a 40 FPS mode in the future. And it sounds like, at least on current gen, that won’t be happening.

Industry observers note that when Rockstar revealed that GTA 6 would target 30 FPS on PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S, some players didn’t take it well. Many had hoped that Rockstar would, like so many other developers this console generation, offer some kind of performance mode. So for some, it was very sad news. But others held out hope that, perhaps in a post-launch update, Rockstar would add in a 60 FPS option or even a 40 FPS option for players enjoying the game on a 120hz TV.

However, Rockstar has confirmed with Kotaku that this isn’t going to happen, even on PS5 Pro. GTA 6 is just too much for these current consoles.

“Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination,” explained Technology Production Director Marc Chambers. “On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”.

I’ve played over 130 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6 on PS5 Pro, and I don’t think the game is worse off for being locked to a framerate of 30 FPS. I’m somewhat of a framerate snob, but the gameplay in GTA 6 works totally fine at 30 fps. And the visuals are truly stunning, and more than make up for the lower framerate.

I know some people might suggest Rockstar turn off ray tracing and other fancy features to offer a 60 FPS option, but it would really take away from what the studio has built. GTA 6 is one of the best-looking games I’ve ever seen and easily sports the best-looking open world I’ve explored in my life. And a lot of that is down to the incredible lighting and ray-tracing tech that can be found in so many different parts of the world. Campfires cast orange, flickering glows on faces. Fancy red sports cars reflect the sunlight, tinting my crappy white car as I drive by them. The lights of my car’s dash and fuel gauge reflect in the windshield of my pickup truck as I cruise around the woods in the dark. Stuff like that adds a lot to the world and the vibes. Removing it would take away so much.

According to recent reports, even if you turn those visual features off, the game is still massive and incredibly alive, with dozens of planes in the air at all times, huge amounts of traffic, and multiple NPCs filling every frame of the game. So I’m not convinced it would be able to hit 60 FPS even with ray-tracing turned off or scaled back.

Sources indicate that and hey, if history is any indicator of the future, this is the worst version of GTA 6 we’ll ever play. The game will almost certainly get ported to PC in the near future and run at 60 FPS or more over there, assuming your rig can run it. Later ports on next-gen machines in the future are also likely coming and will probably feature improved framerate options and more. So if you really want a 60 FPS option in GTA 6, you could just wait. But personally, I’m loving the game even at 30 FPS.

In a recent development, the bigger problem, however? The way the challenge was set up led to all of the other teams working together. Everyone huddled together and gave each other answers like they were cheating on a pop quiz, and then Matt & Michelle had to go it alone. They also had to do both sides of the challenge with no help. Yes, struggling with directions didn’t help, but they were at a heavy disadvantage due to being targeted. The other teams weren’t.

In a recent development, I’m sure TAR would call it fair gameplay. I call it boring TV.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold new directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold new directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day. And it turns out a medieval Call of Duty was also explored at one time.

This latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game. "Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right?" Kurosaki told PC Gamer. "It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty.".

This isn't the first time we've heard of an unusual Call of Duty prototype. When Activision brought Sledgehammer Games into the fold as another lead studio for the lucrative shooter series, the team briefly worked on a third-person horror off-shoot set in Vietnam, which was referred to as Fog of War.

Activision's legal battle with Infinity Ward founders Vince Zampella and Jason West, however, caused the project to be cancelled, as Sledgehammer was roped into helping the studio finish Modern Warfare 3.

As for Kurosaki, he currently leads That's No Moon alongside creative partner Jacob Minkoff and other Infinity Ward and Naughty Dog veterans. The studio is currently working on Crossfire, a narrative-driven third-person shooter set in the universe of Smilegate's free-to-play series of the same name.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Game Awards 2026 has seen the end of the biggest streak in the show's history as no Sony-published game has been nominated for Game of the Year.

In the history of The Game Awards, there have been two years where a PlayStation first party title hasn't been nominated for Game of the Year. 2014, the first year of the show's existence, and now 2026.

Recent findings suggest that sony is also the publisher with the most Game of the Year nominations and wins, getting 14 and three respectively thanks to God of War, The Last of Us Part 2, and Astro Bot. 2018, 2020, and 2022 saw multiple games nominated for the award simultaneously, a feat only matched by Nintendo with two games nominated in 2017 and 2023.

But with 2026, that streak – which started with Bloodborne and is ending with Death Stranding 2 – has come to an end as neither Marathon, Saros, or Marvel's Wolverine have been nominated for Game of the Year. The category is made up of GTA 6, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Resident Evil Requiem, 007 First Light, Phantom Blade Zero, and Control Resonant.

Recent findings suggest that saros and Wolverine did, however, get some nominations. Both Rahul Kohli and Liam McIntyre are up for Best Performance while Saros is up for Best Action Game and Wolverine is up for Innovation in Accessibility.

Recent findings suggest that sony seemed to have a superpower where even the most mid of titles like Horizon: Zero Dawn could nab a nomination over the likes of Resident Evil 7, Yakuza 0, and Nier Automata, or something with as terrible of a third act as Marvel's Spider-Man 2 could beat out Street Fighter 6, Lies of P, Armored Core 6, and Pikmin 4. But with the critical and public reception to Marvel's Wolverine and Marathon, it's perhaps not a shock, and if Returnal didn't get a nomination in a year as quiet as 2021, I would've put money on Saros not making it in a year as stacked as 2026.

GTA 6 Metacritic score makes it the highest-rated game of all time, matching the OG Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

Upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

Word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a firm succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

According to recent reports, bloomberg also report Firaxis have been working on a new XCOM, which is yet to be revealed, but the project has apparently had to contend with numerous development challenges, missing a "significant milestone over the summer." This new XCOM game hasn't been cancelled at the very least, but anonymous sources that spoke with Bloomberg stated it may have to deal with a shakeup due to the cuts. As always, solidarity with all those affected by this situation.

#28119. What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success
