📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that manni L. Perez has been confirmed as the actress behind Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos, just days before the game rolls out.

As spotted by IGN, the confirmation came during The Game Awards' nominations livestream today, where Perez was nominated for Best Performance for her role as co-lead Lucia.

Perez had been widely rumoured to play Lucia for months, and fans have regularly filled her social media livestreams with questions about GTA 6, which she has been oh-so-carefully sidestepping.

Lucia is one half of GTA 6's lead pair alongside Jason Duval, making it the first Grand Theft Auto game with a playable couple.

Jason's actor wasn't among the nominees, so who plays him is still a mystery.

Perez has previously had guest roles in a string of US TV dramas, including Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago P.D., The Blacklist, and Blindspot, and has also done voice work for GTA Online.

Funnily enough, Lucia isn't her first Lucia - she also played Lucia Santiago in a 2023 episode of CBS's East Upcoming York.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

Industry observers note that it's long been revealed that GTA 6 will have a regional release, meaning that some lucky, soon-to-be players will be able to access the game much earlier than others. Rockstar's regional release schedule sees the game launching at midnight on 19th November regardless of what region you're in, and if you wish to join those playing almost a day early, there's the good ol' Xbox Fresh Zealand trick for eager players to try.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping gave its cast a trial by fire. Production on the film – the sixth in the franchise based on Suzanne Collins's novels – kicked off with the very first moment the tributes enter the deadly arena, which certainly put the cast to the test.

When we met with director Francis Lawrence in London, we asked why he wanted to start with such a massive scene – and it turns out the answer is surprisingly practical.

"It's a combo of things. The truth is that when you're shooting over close to 90 days, you have to look at seasons, and we knew that we needed the arena to look a certain way, which meant that we had to shoot at the end of summer to catch the season before it hit fall," he explains (the sequence was filmed in Valle de Lago, Spain).

According to recent reports, "Unfortunately the season earlier, before the summer, was a little dry, and so things weren't as colorful as it was when we scouted in spring. But we started really, primarily, because we needed to shoot it in summer before it got too cold and the weather turned poor," he continues. "And so we started there, and then we made our move to the west of Germany to do District 12, and then we ended in Berlin as we moved into winter, because then it was mostly interior. So, there's a lot of things that go into the scheduling of things, but it does become a fun way of introducing all the upcoming actors into the Hunger Games once they're suddenly there at the Cornucopia and ready to run and fight.".

The Cornucopia is the large, central structure that is stocked with vital supplies and weapons. Usually, running straight for it is reserved for those who can fight or have a particularly strong death wish, since it quickly becomes the site of a brutal bloodbath as tributes are killed in the scrum.

Recent findings suggest that "They see very swiftly how physical making these movies are," Lawrence adds. "I think a lot of people, especially the young ones, when they come into these really underestimate how hard these movies are physically on people.".

Sources indicate that joseph Zada, who plays Haymitch Abernathy – the unlucky tribute of District 12 who is destined to become Katniss Everdeen's mentor – can certainly attest to the difficulty. "It was a crazy place to start at," he tells us. "I barely remember it. I remember snippets of it in my mind. I remember all the cameras being around me and just looking to my left and right and just hyperventilating all day and really hoping that I was doing something. And running, so much running.

"But, just being so scared and worried if I was doing the right job or if I had any idea what character I was playing, or if it was going to work out, and I think over the course of the next three days it did work out," he adds. "But it was actually a really good place to start. It was all the real emotions.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a dark and stormy November night at Gloria Steinem’s townhouse, and Hillary Clinton has something to say about the 2026 election.
  • Recent findings suggest that the former Secretary of State and 2016 presidential candidate is a last-minute but highly anticipated arrival to this dinner honoring Steinem, the late activist.
  • Jihae, Lux Pascal, Naomi Watts, and Bethann Hardison.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a dark and stormy November night at Gloria Steinem’s townhouse, and Hillary Clinton has something to say about the 2026 election. “One of my most anticipated moments will be watching Donald Trump walk into the State of the Union through the now more than one hundred women members of the House of Representatives. I just want them all to stare at him and say, ‘You fired us from jobs we were qualified for. You insulted us. You demeaned our ambition. You undermined our place in government and society. And we’re here.’”.

Huma Abedin, Busy Philips, and Paloma Elsesser.

Recent findings suggest that the former Secretary of State and 2016 presidential candidate is a last-minute but highly anticipated arrival to this dinner honoring Steinem, the late activist. She passed away in September, but the feminist pathfinder was known for throwing these salon-type events (she called them “circles”) at her Upper East Side townhouse, which she bought for just $30,000 in the late ’60s. It’s overflowing with books (I spy Marilyn by Norman Mailer, Jane Fonda’s War by Mary Hershberger, and several Eleanor Roosevelt biographies on the shelves), pictures (there’s one framed of Steinem alongside Mariska Hargitay) and Indian art. (Steinem spent two formative years in the country.) There are magnets in her kitchen of Wonder Woman, Frida Kahlo, and a cloth finger puppet of Hillary Clinton. A political button is pinned to it that claims “Another Bitch for Hillary.” The whole place smells like a Cire Trudon candle, and everyone’s drinking negronis. (Which actually isn’t technically very Steinem—her favorite cocktail was a margarita—but the negronis go with the night’s dinner, prepared by Lilia chef Missy Robbins.) Yet this is one of the first events at the townhouse that Steinem herself isn’t here to lead.

Jihae, Lux Pascal, Naomi Watts, and Bethann Hardison.

Amy Richards, a feminist activist whom many consider to be the daughter Steinem never had—a title Richards rejects because her mentor “didn’t want kids”—stood up at one point to tell the crowd that this is what Steinem would have wanted. Growing up with a transient father and a mentally volatile mother, the late activist took near-obsessive care in maintaining a welcoming home she could share with others. “As long as I knew Gloria, she always said, ‘I just want my home to be the way it’s always been.’ She wanted it to be filled with people,” Richards indicates. “She didn’t grow up with a home. She was traveling the country for the first 10 years of her life and then lived with her mother, who was not very stable.”.

According to recent reports, at least Steinem’s still here on the wall: Months before her death, she posed for a series of portraits by Paola Kudacki for Weldun, a platform that offers physically adaptive and functional fashion. It was a bit of a small miracle that Steinem said yes. “I will say, Gloria did not always love to be photographed,” Richards says. “Especially in her later years—not because of wrinkles or aging, but she was just like, ‘Aren’t there enough pictures of me?’” Weldun and the Gloria Steinem Foundation are presenting tonight’s dinner, and mementos of Steinem are everywhere. On the fireplace mantle sits a pair of her signature Ray-Ban aviators. But Gloria’s stuff isn’t the same as Gloria herself.

Former secretary of state Hillary Clinton hugging Melissa McCarthy.

Industry observers note that which is probably why, in a crowd of women that include Huma Abedin, Mariska Hargitay, Padma Lakshmi, Melissa McCarthy, and Bethann Hardison—who, at the ripe age of 84, shows up wearing Gucci—Clinton’s unexpected arrival feels seismic, like Gloria sent someone in her place. (Hardison tells me she thinks Steinem used whatever divine power she’s got up there to launch the Blue Wave: “She’s probably saying she helped it happen!”) Whatever your views on Clinton’s politics, she was the first woman to receive a presidential nomination from a major party. Paloma Elsesser and I sit crouched in a corner of the room, glued to the window. “There’s mother,” the supermodel whispers to me as Clinton exits her car into the pouring rain and walks up to the townhouse door.

Guests at dinner honoring the late Gloria Steinem.

According to recent reports, “Hi, everybody,” Clinton says as she walks in. The entire dinner comes to a silent halt. “Hi,” the room responds in unison. Madame Secretary doesn’t seem to like the fuss, probably because 30 or so people intensely staring at you when you arrive at a party is objectively unsettling. “Go back to eating!” she says, motioning to the Missy Robbins meal on the table. Clinton sits down next to Naomi Watts and warmly greets Busy Philips, who stumped for Clinton back in 2016. Hargitay blows her a kiss across the table. All anyone wants to do is talk to Clinton about the 2026 election, in which Democrats won at least 55 seats in the Senate and 256 in the House to take both majorities in the US Congress. At the end of the meal—and after a proper catch-up with Shonda Rhimes—Clinton tries to leave, but she can’t. Guests block the door, clamoring to chat her up.

Recent findings suggest that amid the Clinton traffic jam, I ask Hargitay about the photo. She can’t remember exactly what it is from. “Was it Bravo? Was it with Andy…what’s his name?” But she can guess what she thinks Steinem might say about the blue wave: “There is a God!”.

I watch Clinton finally make her exit. It’s late, so I wait several minutes before I descend the stairs to leave too. (I wait for Elsesser, Watts, Hardinn, and Lux Pascal to finish taking a selfie on the steps.) But I spoke too soon: Clinton’s stuck waiting for the coat check, another group of women crowded around her hoping to say something—or, more likely, hoping she states something. With the way this night is going, Clinton might be the last one at the party.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

It has been revealed that "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.".

So, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.
  • The cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter.
  • Sources indicate that its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.

The cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving.

Sources indicate that its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer". The project will continue, but "may face a shakeup as a result of the cuts".

A spokesperson for 2K, the Take-Two label that runs Firaxis, confirmed Hazen's departure to Bloomberg, and stated the studio is "restructuring and recentering around the studio's core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years".

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis," the spokesperson continued. "These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.".

The layoffs come two days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which is developed and published by Rockstar, a separate label at Take-Two.

In September, around 18 months after Civ 7's widely criticised launch - and as the legendary 4X series celebrates its 35th anniversary - Firaxis unveiled a host of newly introduced updates coming to the game as it continued to improve it. These included an atomic age upgrade, dragging Civ 7 into the present and beyond, as well as its first paid expansion, Earthrise, both arriving next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick admitted earlier this year that the studio "got it wrong with Civ 7".

Sources indicate that "The game is a really good game. And it's certainly a profitable enterprise for us. But this is one where I think what we tried to do was a bridge too far, from the consumer's perspective," he told Game File in May.

It’s not the first round of cuts at the studio - 2K confirmed an unspecified number of layoffs at Firaxis in September 2025, and around 30 jobs went in 2023.

I have no idea if this is the case of some reviewers just not being in the target audience of The Hunger Games’ latest prequel Sunrise on the Reaping or if some people who have liked the other movies found this one less moving. But looking at reviews this morning after Sunrise purple carpet photos dropped, I realized not everyone felt the way I did about the 2026 movie release.

According to recent reports, I agree with reviews on one significant point: The adaptation is faithful to Suzanne Collins’ source material, which is a pretty bleak book with a bittersweet ending in the same way the third Hunger Games book is. That’s down to several scenes I personally wanted to see play out on the big screen.

Discussing Film made a significant point to call out the adaptations “faithful” take on the source material. The outlet’s Yasmine Kandil wrote:.

That being said, Sunrise on the Reaping remains exceedingly faithful to the novel’s sequence of events, perhaps more so than any of its predecessors, and often down to the most minute details.

Sources indicate that in fact, I saw that word peppered in and out of reviews. If you liked the book, you should like this movie. Or as Gizmodo's Germain Lussier more than adequately puts it, if you are a fan of this franchise, you'll dig this. It's a "love letter" to fans.

Industry observers note that sunrise on the Reaping, is a love letter to The Hunger Games, filled with connections, explanations, and moments designed to provide maximum delight to fans of the series. It isn’t concerned with setting up the world or reexplaining the stakes. It says, 'This is the sixth movie. If you’re watching this without context, well, that’s on you.'.

Still, when it comes to SOME of these reviews, I feel like I watched a completely different movie.

At Indiewire, the grade was a C- (with a bright spot in Jesse Plemons’ performance as Plutarch), and this comment from Ryan Lattanzio is really sticking with me after perusing reviews.

Sunrise on the Reaping is a dreary slog, another death-march “They Shoot Horses, Don’t They?” riff with a pretty Gen Z cast, and one that mistakes upcoming layers of darkness (and trauma!) for the sort of profundity that its filmmakers hope will burnish a creatively withering property.

Industry observers note that the Guardian was equally unenthusiastic about the movie, and had seemingly a lot of fun lambasting it, calling it “overwrought” and “boring,” and even making fun of the flick’s name. ( I think Peter Bradshaw’s review highlights my earlier point, that this movie isn’t for every demographic.).

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Here is yet another iteration of the utterly exhausted, unbearably extended and now surreally boring Hunger Games franchise, based on the YA bestsellers by Suzanne Collins. This one has another of the series’ convoluted faux-mythic subtitles: Sunrise on the Reaping. What, “harvest dawn” not old-timey enough?

These aren’t the only two bad reviews, they are just among the more brutal and trending. (Though it's worth pointing out plenty of outlets, like THR, Time Out and more gave the film positive reviews, and it is at the time of this writing, trending positively on review aggregators.).

Recent findings suggest that honestly, is Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping perfect? No. Mckenna Grace and Jesse Plemons are standouts, and Elle Fanning and Joseph Zada do fine jobs, but I’m not bringing up Oscars here. I also think because the movie is so long, some of the emotional deaths in the arena are blunted, and I wish we had more time with characters like Maysilee, Wiress, Beetee and Ampert.

It has been revealed that regardless, this movie made me feel a lot of feelings about humanity, and what humans are willing to endure. Haymitch’s story ties in so hard with Katness,’ and the end cap OG Hunger Games scene where she was able to do what he could not was both hopeful and sad at the same time. This movie emotionally wrecked me. I cried multiple times. If you are a fan of the franchise at all, you should see it on the major screen. It’s proven to be a franchise with staying power and (hopefully) more stories to tell.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I've pretty much always carried an annoying, tense pain on the right side of my neck.
  • But I should have had more faith in this sage, sage advice, because (alongside a renewed exercise routine to support it), the simple change to my setup actually did make a massive difference to my shoulder and neck pain.
  • The TLDR here is that Secretlab's Vertical Monitor stand was all I needed to stop the constant strain of tension in my neck.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've pretty much always carried an annoying, tense pain on the right side of my neck. And when I say always, I'm 29, and I remember going to see a physiotherapist about it when I was 18 - so you're talking my entire adult life. I tried everything: workouts, stretches, posture improvements, so you can probably imagine the mocking laugh that came out of me when, earlier this year, an ergonomics doctor at the Secretlab HQ told me all I needed was to switch my monitors around a bit.

But I should have had more faith in this sage, sage advice, because (alongside a renewed exercise routine to support it), the simple change to my setup actually did make a massive difference to my shoulder and neck pain. The only issue? The Secretlab products I needed to make it happen aren't the cheapest, but since they're now seeing discounts in the Black Friday Secretlab sale, I figure it's a good time to tell the story.

The TLDR here is that Secretlab's Vertical Monitor stand was all I needed to stop the constant strain of tension in my neck. If you want to skip the story and check it out on your own, it's available now in Secretlab's Black Friday or End-of-Year sale.

Industry observers note that I met Dr. Lindsey “GamerDoc” Migliore at the Secretlab Singapore office back in April when I was invited to get a special early look at the then unannounced Secretlab Atlas. Myself and a few other UK journos were treated to an ergonomics session with Dr. Lindsey, a licensed physician and Esports medicine specialist who works with Esports athletes and organizations to optimize health and performance across both competitive and casual gaming.

In a recent development, throughout the session, she made her way around the group, giving us a free clinic of sorts as we asked about our aches and pains and how we might improve our setups to remedy them. She roasted PCGamer's Jacob Ridley over his sitting position, but Secretlab's PR folks rapidly pointed her at me because they knew I had an annoying pain in my neck.

Industry observers note that seeing as Dr. Lindsey applies principles of sports science, ergonomics, and performance medicine to gaming setups and actual Esports athletes, I was hoping for some technical, in-depth advice. Instead, she simply asked, "Do you have more than one monitor?".

"Yeah," I said, "I have one main one, and then a vertical one over on the right-hand side for Slack, Spotify, and other smaller apps when I'm working.".

"And your pain is on which side?" she asked.

"The right," I replied, pensively.

Sources indicate that "You should try and put your secondary monitor up above your main one," Dr. Lindsey stated with a smile. "That way, you won't be constantly craning your neck to the right and holding so much tension on that side".

In a recent development, I paused for a moment as I heard smirks emerging in the group. My eyebrows dropped, my eyes squinted. There's no way it's that simple, I thought to myself. Laughing it off, I retorted, "You sound crazy right now.".

It was probably very disrespectful, but months later, after Secretlab called my bluff and supplied me with its various monitor arms to try, I feel like a total idiot.

Luckily, Dr. Lindsey took my feedback with great humour (even referring to me as a Celtic Jon Snow at one point), but for the record, I'd like to formally apologise for not taking her word as bond.

Recent findings suggest that turns out, stacking one monitor on top of the other made a world of difference, and despite the higher cost of Secretlab's vertical monitor stand, it's something I'd highly recommend to anyone who has more than one monitor on their gaming desk and struggles with similar pain to me. Lifting your head up to look at a monitor above your main eyeline is a much healthier repeated movement than constantly looking over to one direction - and no matter how good their head and neck support is, none of the best gaming chairs will change that.

I've now been using this monitor configuration for at least five or six months, and the difference in the neck pain I carry is massive. Thankfully, even though I don't own a Secretlab Magnus desk, I'm still able to make the brand's monitor arms work for me because they're compatible with other worktops so long as they meet the minimum thickness requirements for clamping them down securely.

Now, it should be mentioned that alongside this monitor change, I've been doing a lot of exercise and gym work, which has no doubt done just as much to help things, so keep that in mind. I'm a firm believer that no one desk, monitor arm, or gaming chair is enough to cure your aches and pains without you putting in work alongside them.

According to recent reports, since originally taking on the vertical monitor stand and attaching both of my monitors to it, I've taken on a heavier OLED monitor as my main one, so I've also had to incorporate Secretlab's Heavy Duty Monitor Arm (also discounted in the Black Friday sale) to accommodate more than an 8kg load. It's a real shame you can't mix and match these. It'd be really cool if you could attach the stronger arm from the Heavy Duty variant to the vertical monitor stand, for example. Still, I can understand why the two aren't physically compatible.

Sources indicate that the only other hesitation I have about Secretlab's vertical monitor stand is that it's expensive. For context, there are plenty listed at Amazon, like Standopia's and AVLT's which come in at $79.99 at Amazon and $99.99 at Amazon respectively.

Recent findings suggest that yes, with Secretlab's, you can attach all sorts to it if you wish. With room for four Doc Ock-like limbs extending out from it, you could have four monitors like a stock broker, two monitors and a tablet or music stand of some description, maybe a camera, or whatever you can make work. But even grabbing it with just two arms, it's a very pricey desk attachment. That's why I've chosen my moment to recommend it to you a little cheaper during Secretlab's Black Friday sale. If your budget can stretch to this monitor configuration with its small discount, I'd recommend it. Especially with Secretlab's build quality giving you peace of mind. If not, there are loads of cheaper alternatives linked below.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games.
  • In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time.
  • Industry observers note that the original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a latest developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

Industry observers note that the original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

It has been revealed that raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

Industry observers note that gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the upcoming team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Avril Lavigne is now a mom. The 42-year-old Canadian might count songs like "Here's to Never Growing Up" among her hits, but in news posted to Instagram Friday, Avril Lavigne revealed a very grown-up milestone.

Beneath a carousel of three black-and-white photos, Lavigne wrote “Our Mini Fucking Princess has arrived,” followed by emojis depicting a baby bottle, a crown, and a pink heart and bow. One photo demonstrates Lavigne cradling an infant dressed in an animal-print onesie and matching headband, while another shows three pairs of Vans on a skateboard. No other details, including information on the baby's name or if Lavigne has a co-parent, were provided.

Avril Lavigne at the Viper Room in the early 2000s.

A spokesperson for the singer told People that “Avril has been enjoying time with her family while working on her newly introduced album and wants to thank the fans for all of their love!”.

Industry observers note that lavigne has been married twice: once to Canadian guitarist Deryck Whibley and then to Chad Kroeger, the Canadian frontman of the band Nickelback. That latter partnership ended in 2018, but in 2022 she almost tied the knot a third time, with rapper Mod Sun. That relationship ended in 2023.

Mod Sun and Avril Lavigne attend the 2022 MTV Video Music Awards on August 28, 2022.

One constant in Lavigne's life has been strong bond she shares with her parents. When, in May 2025, she brought her mother on stage at Madison Square Garden, she wrote on social media: “Ever since I was a little girl, both my mom and dad saw something in me and encouraged me to practice very hard and pursue my dream of becoming a singer/ musician. They made a lot of sacrifices for me and I could not be where I am today without them.”.

In a recent development, continuing, she wrote, “I am grateful to both my parents. Thank you for everything, I love you both!”.

Industry observers note that lavigne was still a teenager when her parents allowed her to leave high school to pursue her dream, and her debut at age 17 was a smash hit. Her success continued with singles including 2002's chart-topper “Complicated" and 2021 song “Bite Me.”.

Industry observers note that though Friday's announcement was a surprise to most, Lavigne has never been quiet about her desire to become a mom when the time is right. Speaking with E! News in 2013, she laid out her initiative: "I want one or two [kids], but not right now," the then-29-year old said. "Like, in the future. Eventually.".

Courtney Howard, a writer for Variety and other outlets, calls the movie a great “hang out” film, giving flowers to Pitt and his co-stars Elizabeth Debicki and Peter Weller:.

This seems to be another one of those. Clayton Davis, another Variety writer, also calls it one:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in a first substantial update since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have unveiled some additions coming to the community-run backend database.
  • "We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick revision on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in a first substantial update since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have unveiled some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.

"We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick revision on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.

Sources indicate that there are two main upcoming features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon. The first is one that anyone could have seen coming, a new tab on each moddable game's page that reveals off some mods hosted for it on Nexus Mods and a host of modding-related data. "The new tab will help you discover mods for games you're browsing on SteamDB, making it easier to see whether a game has an active modding community and explore what it has to offer," Fomann wrote. "For now, we'll only be showing mods from Nexus Mods, as we already have access to that wealth of modding data, making it a straightforward starting point for this new feature.

"We appreciate that some of you might be wondering why we're not including Steam Workshop, too. It's certainly something we'd be open to exploring as we develop the feature further, along with other modding sources. With that in mind, if you run a modding website and would be interested in having your community's mods included, we'd love to hear from you.".

According to recent reports, that seems perfectly fine, but the other incoming feature's a bit more controversial given SteamDB's historically not been all about the money. "One thing we've seen people ask for is an easier way to find the cheapest place to buy a game, and we're now working on making that possible," Folmann wrote. "We'll be introducing affiliate links to authorised game retailers, giving you more options when looking for the best available price on a game.

"We recognise that introducing affiliate links may raise some concerns, so we want to be clear about how they'll work. First and foremost, as I mentioned, we'll only feature authorised retailers; we will not be including grey-market resellers. We've also made a deliberate decision about how prices are displayed: retailers will be ordered by the cheapest available price in your currency, not by whichever retailer offers us the highest affiliate commission. If a retailer doesn't offer pricing in your currency, we'll still show deals in other currencies provided they are available in your region.".

Sources indicate that folmann was clear in the initial announcement of the takeover that Nexus Mods' bosses would be actively looking into ways SteamDB could make more money to sustain itself, so the addition of these links isn't out of the blue either. Whether SteamDB regulars agree that they're a "lighter-touch" way of earning the site some cash without detracting from the traditional experience of using it is another matter. I'll need to see how I feel once I've actually navigated a few pages with the links in as part of looking up stuff about games, but my first instinct is that as long as the pages don't end up revolving around the links and it's still easy to get to the info you want without interacting with them, I probably won't be too put out.

Beyond those tweaks, Folmann mentioned "improvements to how updates are tested before they go live" and how quickly the team can react to issues have been among the less obvious work going on behind the scenes. "We're still in the early stages of what we want to achieve, and there's plenty more work we need to do and would like to work on," he wrote in closing.

Folmann and co only took over Nexus Mods in June last year, making them still relatively fresh custodians of both it and SteamDB.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.
  • It has been revealed that "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business.
  • According to recent reports, feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.

It has been revealed that "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business. "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar launched Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it.".

According to recent reports, feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games. Feder added, "My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West. In the East, they've already accepted it.".

Feder, who currently heads up venture capital fund Tirta Ventures, is investing in AI-first games. He, however, doesn't necessarily believe AI will reduce development costs, but that it also offers other advantages that could help game makers keep up with shifting consumer tastes.

In a recent development, "A lot of incumbents think about AI as a way of reducing costs, which it is," Feder said. "I query whether it will actually reduce costs, or will it just make games bigger for the same cost? But we're more interested in what AI can do to radically change gameplay.".

It has been revealed that feder views gen-AI simply as latest technology that allows developers to do things they couldn't before. He likened it to Unreal Engine's instancing technology, which allowed Fortnite and other battle royale games to support 100+ players in a single server.

"That's question number one as we think about what we invest in: Was this possible before AI?" Feder stated of his VC firm's strategy. "And when AI gets better, does the game get better? That's harder for an incumbent to focus on, because they deploy a lot of capital, have enormous advantages in terms of distribution, capital, and IP, and all of that needs to be protected.".

There's been enormous pushback from players, developers and pundits against the use of gen-AI in games. Even so, more and more studios have revealed using some gen-AI during development, such as to assist with coding. More broadly, gen-AI adoption is on the rise across the industry, with a recent report estimating 40 percent of developers are using it.

Some development studios, such as Fortnite maker Epic Games, have doubled down on the use of gen-AI in game development. Epic is even more bullish on gen-AI in its Unreal Engine, which the company is currently transforming into an engine that's almost entirely driven by gen-AI and LLMs. Consumer sentiment remains sour, however, and the perception of the tool is not helped by the number of 'AI slop' games taking over Steam's storefront, the 'enshittification' of fan wikis, or the link AI seems to have to the unprecedented wave of layoffs that has shaken the industry over the past two years.

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 features the largest open world Rockstar has ever created. It’s a map filled with locations to explore. However, after playing over 130 hours of GTA 6, there were still plenty of locations, including a zoo and a small northern town, that I never visited once during the story. And according to Rockstar, that’s because the map in GTA 6 was built for the “future.”.

Ahead of Grand Theft Auto 6‘s launch, I asked Rockstar about the inclusion of at least two large casinos on the map. These locations can’t be entered and are never referenced or visited in the story or in any of the side missions I played. So I asked why Rockstar didn’t let Jason and Lucia bet it all on red.

âJason and Luciaâs story didnât feel like the right place for us to introduce gambling,” explained Rockstar VP of design Stephen Donkin. “Especially with the fine balance we sought throughout the economy.”.

That’s fair. GTA 6 is the first Grand Theft Auto game to really make money feel important, and at times it can be hard to scrounge together enough cash to buy a upcoming gun or fix up your car. So letting players save-scum their way to victory at the casino and have the characters come away with tens of thousands of dollars or more could have derailed the story Rockstar was trying to tell. But those casinos and other unused locations, like an extremely detailed zoo and a large graveyard, could end up being used for…something in the future.

Industry observers note that “The map has been built for the long term and with many factors in mind,” noted Donkin. “So there are a few areas on the map that give us options in the future should we have a gameplay or narrative need for them.â.

Rockstar didn’t share any more details with me about what those “needs” could be, but it does seem that the company has built GTA 6 as something it can expand upon over time, possibly with expansions, updates, and/or some kind of online mode. For now, there’s plenty of GTA 6 for players to get lost in, and even those out-of-the-way locations are fun to explore.

It's weird to type this out, but the GTA 6 release is finally upon us after a 13-year wait.

Red Dead Redemption 2 introduced to acclaim at the time to ease the wait, though few things in gaming feel as significant an event as a Grand Theft Auto release from Rockstar.

It has been revealed that and thankfully, the wait looks to be worth it. The GamesRadar+ GTA 6 review lands on a perfect score, and says "Rockstar hasn't just set a fresh benchmark, it has delivered the highest-fidelity sandbox of the generation." It's not just us, either. The GTA 6 Metacritic score is a good 'un. In fact, only the OG Zelda: Ocarina of Time can match it.

Sources indicate that so, we're probably on the same page. It's time to get the download going, and thoughts to our gaming brethren on PC who don't own a console.

To celebrate the moment, we're firing up the live blog to put everything you need to know in one, evolving space – from review buzz to launch requirements to exactly how the GTA 6 release time rollout is working. On that note, let's crack on.

"It’s hard not to worry": Even as GTA 6 releases on console amid glowing reviews, Rockstar devs are already concerned about getting laid off

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining.
  • In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".
  • Industry observers note that the animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 launches on console today. It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining. And yet, staff at Rockstar Games are apparently worrying about being laid off, as development winds down and investors start to bicker about Line Going Up Even More.

In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

Industry observers note that the animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section. Following some personal reflections on his time at the studio, he calls on other Rockstar devs to get behind the union, describing it as both "a huge step forward" for a company that has previously faced allegations of "crunch culture", and a win for UK game developers at large. "What happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more," Uriarte writes.

The vote at Rockstar North will run till 26th November, and could give rise to a union spanning over 1600 developers, according to umbrella organisation the Independent Workers of Great Britain. If that comes to pass, it would make the Rockstar union the largest recognised videogame developer union in the UK.

It comes as the company and a group of fired workers await the result of an employment tribunal battle over alleged "union-busting". Rockstar has accused the workers in question of "gross misconduct" and a breach of confidentiality by means of a union Discord server. Amongst other things, the legal brawl has revealed that Rockstar had a mole on that server for two and a half years, prior to the firings.

As for the prospect of further job losses, after GTA 6 goes on sale, Uriarte cites a wave of mass layoffs across the industry that has affected the creators of even commercially successful games like Battlefield 6 and Netflix's FIFA World Cup.

"After the massive day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds," he writes. "Studios across the industry have been slashing huge portions of their workforces, with an estimated 24,000 roles axed globally over the last two years. It states a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

Recent findings suggest that the obvious context here is that GTA 6 has been a massively expensive production, with a development team headcount in the thousands. While one could accuse Uriarte of fear-mongering, I do find it hard to believe that executives at parent organization Take-Two aren't weighing up some timely "down-sizing" right now. In general, videogame companies have a long tradition of axing the books once a game has been shipped, despite arguments that keeping experienced teams intact often pays off. In Rockstar's case, however, it's also worth bearing in mind that the GTA 6 rolling out this week is only part of the package. There's also the hazy prospect of the next incarnation of GTA Online, which – going by GTA 5 sales – will be a money spinner for many years, and will require a sizeable staff to maintain. Oh, and of course there's the PC version.

Echoing many peers, Uriarte also argues in his piece that it's crucial to unionise now to secure protection against generative AI cost-cutting initiatives.

In a recent development, "The rapid emergence of AI is transforming how studios work and raising fundamental questions about the future of our industry," he continues. "Across the sector, the skills that workers spend years developing risk being devalued as their creative work is replaced by AI. Rockstar has noted it is committed to preserving jobs and it has been clear that our games will continue to be made by people. But with recognition we’d have a seat at the table to manage this industry-wide transition together.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard.
  • Sources indicate that for those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the latest late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold.
  • It has been revealed that there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard. Suspensions have been issued, trade locks have been put on accounts, and ill-gotten gold is being seized.

Sources indicate that for those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the latest late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold. By promptly clearing select mobs with area-of-effect damage, players would loot upwards of 100 raw gold an hour. This exploit, clearly not intentional, was nonetheless farmed until Blizzard hotfixed it earlier in the week.

It has been revealed that there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit. That speculation would come to an end late last night with an official statement from the World of Warcraft: Forever development team.

In a recent development, "As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced," the statement reads. "Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

It goes on to explain the nature of the bug that made this gold farm possible, before reassuring those who may have accidentally benefited from some extra cash from their regular runs of Blackmaw Hold they have nothing to worry about. The same cannot be said for those who took advantage of the situation.

Industry observers note that "Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug," it continues. "But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

In a recent development, "Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers.".

Recent findings suggest that the post concludes by thanking players for their feedback on the matter, and a final warning: "As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse.".

This decision certainly sets the precedent moving forward with World of Warcraft: Forever that such exploits won't be tolerated, and rolling back the wealth of those who made out of Blackmaw Hold like bandits is a good measure that should prevent continuous damage.

Inevitably the exploit would have had some impact, specifically in those days prior to trading blocks being put in place. While the gold on the exploiter's accounts may be removed, any purchases they made on the in-game auction house will have affected others through buying and selling goods with ample funds.

Those who were suspended temporarily will be able to regain access to the game by the time the first wave of raids come out in December, so it very much feels like a firm slap on the wrist in that regard. Even so, given the establishment of punishments for such behavior, one can only wonder if future events will come with harsher penalties.

Sources indicate that world of Warcraft: Forever, despite this small economic roadbump, is proving exceptionally popular for Blizzard. It's already broken records for the series, and has impressed players so far with its revamping of the classic MMO.

While La Bola Negra continues to amass various accolades and early awards, like the Best Director award at this year's Cannes Film Festival and the Audience Award at the Toronto International Film Festival, directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo are extra grateful and overwhelmed by the film's reception and success in their home country of Spain.

Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

It has been revealed that “You can't plan the miracle,” Calvo said during a panel conversation moderated by Ricky Martin at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. “We’ve done many projects and each one of them has, they've all been good, but you never know when it's going to happen. And with La Bola Negra, we thought it was a very specific story and we thought that our audience was going to like it, but we never knew it was going to hit everyone. I think it's about to become the second highest grossing movie in the history of Spain. For me, the most beautiful part of it is the videos of the people hugging after the screenings, giving tissues to each other, comforting each other.”.

According to recent reports, la Bola Negra follows several gay men whose lives are bound together by their identities, love and loss, and the looming presence of the Spanish Civil War. The acclaimed Spanish language drama spans nearly a century and stars Miguel Bernardeau, Álvaro Lafuente Calvo (the singer known as Guitarricadelafuente) in his first major acting role, Carlos Gonzalez, Milo Quifes and Penélope Cruz.

Guitarricadelafuente at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

Following an exclusive screening of the film on Friday, Martin moderated a panel conversation featuring directors Ambrossi and Calvo, and stars Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente and Bernardeau. Calvo remarked they are all riding high on the positive audience reactions and reception. “Creating this sense of community and hearing people saying, ‘This movie changed me. It really made me understand things about me.’ The power that art has, we forget it, but then this happens and … the rest is a dream. The rest we're living is a dream.”.

The directors also consider having Cruz play a small but pivotal role in the film to be part of their living a dream. When Martin asked Cruz how her longstanding allyship to the LGBTQ+ community shaped her intention or performance, she mentioned, “I don't even ask myself that question because it's such a part of me, of the way that I was raised. My very young parents, my parents had me when they were 21. It was a house where the values were about respect and it was just like breathing. They didn't even have to sit us down and give us a lecture about it, it was the way my family was living by example. And on top of that, then I had my other master Pedro Almodóvar who I've worked with for seven movies. And I always remember growing up thinking, why is he not the president of our country? Because he was huge in a time where his presence was really necessary, not only through his films, but also by the things that he was saying. So I feel like all of that has shaped me.”.

Miguel Bernardeau, Guitarricadelafuente, Penélope Cruz, Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi and Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

She continued: “So when I have in my hands the possibility of playing somebody like Nené Romero, that is a reminder that unfortunately not everyone in the world feels the way we feel about everyone having a right for respect, everyone having a right to be themselves.”.

Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

For Martin, a Bola Negra superfan who admitted he was nervous to be asking questions instead of answering them, the actor and musician mentioned he found out about his hosting opportunity only the day before and despite the nerves couldn't pass up the opportunity to help celebrate the film.

Sources indicate that “I usually answer the questions, I never ask the questions, but I needed to be here,” he told the audience. “I saw this film and for a while I was in the movie. I was really touched. The acting, the way it was written, people are crying because that's just the way it is, [really moving].”.

Miguel Bernardeau at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

It has been revealed that the inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in Latest York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robert Pattinson has had a pretty ridiculous year. Between The Drama, Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, and the upcoming Dune: Part Three on the 2026 movie schedule, he's been keeping busy. Now, as if playing the Dark Knight wasn't enough, he's officially been cast as the next James Bond. Naturally, the announcement has generated plenty of reactions, but I wasn't expecting Jon Stewart to have one of the funniest takes I've heard so far.

During Monday night's episode of The Daily Show, Stewart addressed the Bond casting while discussing a string of technological disasters and travel disruptions that had made headlines over the weekend. Somehow, he wove them all into an increasingly ridiculous story about how he was supposed to audition for 007. The lengths he went to before revealing that the Twilight franchise breakout star had beaten him to the role had me laughing out loud. Stewart joked:.

It has been revealed that I was supposed to fly out to a gig. An audition, actually. Kind of a major one. And obviously, delays at the airport. No big deal. I just thought, well, I'll just go by my preferred travel method, Mississippi riverboat.

Recent findings suggest that when your flight gets canceled, logic dictates that the next step is to hop aboard a riverboat. Obviously. Unfortunately for Stewart, his backup transportation wasn't particularly reliable either, and things only got worse when he tried to contact the people running the audition. He continued the bit:.

It has been revealed that unfortunately, we also ran into a bit of a... well, it ran into us, but... so I just thought, well, I'll let the production know I was going to be late by sending them an email from my beloved Microsoft Outlook account. And then the... uh... which... it would have been fine, as long as I could still electronically withdraw the money to rent a car, which... long story short, they ended up giving the role to [BLEEP] Robert Pattinson.

I was already laughing at the idea of Stewart missing out on a big role because his riverboat ran into trouble and Microsoft Outlook wasn't cooperating. But he saved his best complaint for last, taking problem with the fact that Pattinson already has another pretty famous character on his résumé. Raising his fist in mock frustration, the longtime late-night host shouted:.

According to recent reports, pattinson! You already got Batman. Enough's enough!

I mean, he's got a point. How many iconic characters does one guy need? Here's an actor who has already played Edward Cullen in the Twilight movies, Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter, and Bruce Wayne in The Batman. Now he's adding 007 to the résumé. At this rate, I half expect someone to announce him as the next Superman. Hey, with James Gunn’s recent outing anything is possible.

In a recent development, of course, Stewart was having fun with the news, and I don't think anybody seriously believes Pattinson should be disqualified from playing Bond because he's already Batman. But I do think it's funny that the actor is becoming the face of another enormous franchise while he's still working on The Batman: Part II.

In a recent development, pattinson's casting as James Bond was officially unveiled Monday, following years of speculation about who would replace Daniel Craig. The upcoming 26th Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, who also worked with the Die My Darling actor on Dune: Part Three. While plenty of actors were rumored to be in contention, Pattinson ultimately landed the role. The announcement has already generated strong reactions from fans, which is hardly surprising given how attached people are to the franchise.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Recent findings suggest that personally, I'm curious to see what he brings to Bond. He's spent years choosing interesting projects and taking roles that don't always seem like the obvious next step for somebody who became famous playing a sparkly vampire. His Batman was a particularly interesting take on Bruce Wayne, and I wouldn't be surprised if he approached 007 with the same willingness to make the character his own. Although now I also kind of want to hear him deliver the famous Bond introduction in his Batman voice.

Robert Pattinson's first James Bond movie doesn't have a release date yet, although production is expected to begin sometime in 2027. Meanwhile, The Batman: Part II is presently scheduled for February 2028.

Personally, I think it would be hilarious if Pattinson's next role was playing Jon Stewart in a biopic. Stranger things have happened in Hollywood, and at this point, Stewart might want to keep an eye on those casting announcements.

Industry observers note that in the meantime, you can catch Stewart hosting The Daily Show Mondays at 11 p.m. ET on Comedy Central, with latest episodes available to stream the following morning with a Paramount+ subscription.

It has been revealed that after Jensen Huang's departure from the manufacturer last week, Nvidia is now on the hunt for its next permanent CEO. Speaking in the Q&A section of Nvidia's Q3 2027 earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones states the directors are taking the search "very seriously.".

"We're going to look into internal candidates as well as external candidates" claims Jones. "The board appreciates that we're living in a world where the advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace. Our new CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully.".

Jones also notes the manufacturer "won't expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person," but Amazon boss Jeff Bezos seems to think that hiring outside of Nvidia would be a mistake.

"If you don't bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider," states Bezos, speaking at the Silicon Valley & The World conference on Tuesday (via Yahoo Finance). "Nvidia is too complicated. I think outside CEOs in complex companies have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding, and so I would always think that's a last resort.".

Nvidia is presently being helmed by CFO Collette Kress as an interim chief, while recent reports have suggested that Huang may make a potential return to the company.

The ex-Nvidia chief said that he would come back "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the organization, and America" after a petition calling for his reinstatement, but Nvidia's board has poured cold water on this idea already.

"The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," indicates Jones during the earnings call opening statements.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Latest Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early.

"One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the Latest Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

For those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to Upcoming Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result.

Microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 Upcoming Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it.

Sources indicate that if you aren't keen on doing so for whatever reason, you can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 too. If you want one final run through on what to expect from Rockstar's big release last minute, our Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 page should set you right for good measure.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that if you’ve played any of the mainline Grand Theft Auto games, you’ve likely committed a crime and heard a police radio communication reporting your naughty behavior.
  • Sources indicate that early on in Grand Theft Auto 6, Jason’s hacker friend and stoner buddy Cal does the character a solid.
  • Industry observers note that now, to be clear, I don’t think Rockstar needed to dedicate any time or effort to explaining how players could hear police radio chatter in GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

Sources indicate that if you’ve played any of the mainline Grand Theft Auto games, you’ve likely committed a crime and heard a police radio communication reporting your naughty behavior. It’s been a part of the series since the first game. And yet, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the first game in the series to actually explain how your character can hear this police chatter.

Sources indicate that early on in Grand Theft Auto 6, Jason’s hacker friend and stoner buddy Cal does the character a solid. He grabs his phone and installs a custom, homebrew police radio scanner program. From then on, Jason can hear the police reporting on his actions, crimes, and location, as was the case in (nearly) every previous GTA game. Later on, when GTA 6 lets you free-roam around as Lucia, she, too, has the same police scanner app installed on her phone. The game doesn’t show Cal installing it, so I’ll just assume it happened off-camera.

Industry observers note that now, to be clear, I don’t think Rockstar needed to dedicate any time or effort to explaining how players could hear police radio chatter in GTA. Sure, sometimes I’d think about how it was possible for characters like CJ or Tommy Vercetti to hear the police reporting on their crimes, but then I would just remind myself it’s a video game, and games are filled with stuff that doesn’t make sense. Characters die and then respawn. Protagonists never age. And you can hear the police radio chatter despite not having a scanner. Just usual video game-y nonsense.

Still, I think it’s fun that for GTA 6, Rockstar took the time to explain how Jason and Lucia can hear the police radio chatter. And it also factors into gameplay. Our protagonists know if the police have spotted their car or have reported their clothing. They even mention it during chases as they try to make their escape, so it’s vital we understand that the characters, and not just the player, can hear the chatter. In past games, you could just assume it was a gameplay mechanic, and the protagonists didn’t hear the radio messages. Not so in GTA 6.

I guess Rockstar felt like it was finally necessary to provide a grounded explanation for this classic GTA feature.Â I await Rockstar explaining why every state in the GTA universe is an island in Grand Theft Auto 7.Â.

I've never been so impressed by a person entering a car in a video game before.

Slay the Spire 2 is one of this year's best selling games despite only being available on PC, and its players are "obsessed"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (483 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that one million copies for each month on sale, it seems.
  • That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.
  • In a recent development, slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that one million copies for each month on sale, it seems. Slay the Spire 2, Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder, is estimated to have sold 7.9m copies since its release in Steam Early Access in March.

That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.

In a recent development, slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox. That is notable, as the game is only out on Steam, meaning it has sold enough copies to outpace games on platforms it's not even available on.

We already knew Slay the Spire 2 was one of the year's biggest releases. In its first week on sale, the game sold over 3m copies. It quickly became March's top-selling game on Steam, beating blockbuster competition in Crimson Desert and Resident Evil Requiem. Slay the Spire 2, alongside other indie titles such as Meccha Chameleon, have helped Steam deliver another record year of revenue.

It was such a hit, even, that other indie developers felt it negatively impacted sales of their own games. Mewgenics maker Edmund McMillen recently told Eurogamer "it sucked everybody out". "The same players who liked Mewgenics, they were Slay The Spire players. So they all went woosh and right over," McMillen said.

Slay the Spire 2 has been consistently popular with players, too, and that popularity has seemingly continued. Elliott noted the game never fell below 2.5 million active players each month since March.

According to recent reports, slay the Spire 2's loyal following also meant that the recently released beta patch, which added a new character, was enough to bring back millions of players. Despite only being available for players who opt into the beta branch of the game, Slay the Spire 2 more than doubled its daily active users to reach its highest daily player count in six months.

Sources indicate that "Simply put: Slay the Spire 2 players are obsessed," wrote Elliott. "And it's not just a niche group of dedicated players, either. The average play time is nearly 84 hours, sure. But zooming out, 1.9 million folks have played for over 100 hours.".

Incidentally, nearly 100,000 players bought the game but never played it, which Elliott added could explain the discrepancy between player numbers and copies sold.

According to recent reports, looking ahead, Slay the Spire 2's road to version 1.0 is expected to be long, with several features and gameplay additions still in the works. Then there are the console ports, which have yet to be announced, but are very much expected.

In Eurogamer's Slay the Spire 2 early access review, Bertie Purchese called it "a deceptively familiar sequel" whose confident design and smart new additions build on what made the original work so well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a very, very big game with tons of main missions, side missions, activities, random events, races, and more to find and complete. So you might feel compelled to clear out the map before reaching the finale. But you don’t need to do that.

In a recent development, in past Rockstar Games, like GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2, the studio has let players return to the open world after finishing the main story. However, how this has been handled has varied. In RDR2, you take on the role of another character who can complete activities and side missions after the credits roll. In GTA IV, the game just lets you keep playing post-credits as Niko. This is how it works in most GTA games, actually. Things are a bit different in GTA 6.

Instead, before you enter the final mission, which took me about 90 hours or so to reach in my playthrough, the game makes a big point of asking if you want to go forward with the finale or not. Once you wrap up that big, multi-mission finale and see one of the game’s main endings, GTA 6 tosses you back in time to that moment when you were asked if you wanted to finish the story or not. But this time, Jason and Lucia say no; they aren’t ready, and head back out into Vice City. At that point, you can keep playing GTA 6, wrap up everything on the map, and explore. (The finale mission marker remains on the map if you want to finish the game again and possibly get a different ending.).

It’s an interesting way to handle the endgame and is unlike any past Grand Theft Auto. It also lets GTA 6‘s ending go in a lot of different directions, depending on your choices. I’m not going to even hint at what those endings are, but I’ve seen two of them and trust me, they play out in wildly different and sometimes surprising ways.

The one downside to this approach is that GTA 6 feels a bit frozen in time at the end of the game. No upcoming major storylines can be introduced, as they would possibly get in the way of the narrative wrapping up.

Sources indicate that but hey, once you beat the final mission, you unlock the ability to reach 100 percent completion and even unlock the ability to complete challenges to reveal in-game cheat codes that let you go wild in Vice City. So consider it a vacation for Jason and Lucia after all your hard work as a criminal.

It's been part of GTA for decades, but never explained.

Rockstar North head of production Rob Nelson shares the last bits and bobs that made it into GTA 6.

The studio also explained why you can't gamble in GTA 6 despite a casino being included on the map.

Grand Theft Auto 6 doesnât feature satirical websites because the emphasis was on social media and phone apps.

GTA 6 is presently neck-and-neck with the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as Metacritic's best reviewed game ever.

The massive open-world game features its own social media network complete with a GTA joke.
