📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year. In the aftermath of her win, Svedberg-Yen dropped a pretty big bombshell: she's no longer with the game's developer, Sandfall Interactive.

Industry observers note that "No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the tech giant. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a fresh generation of video game narrative designers.

Recent findings suggest that "One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.".

In a recent development, her motivation for this initiative? Simply, she wants to change how the industry works. "I've discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it's a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations.".

According to recent reports, "The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help," she added later. "That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don't know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.".

Recent findings suggest that sandfall Interactive previously mentioned its guiding "North Star" will always be its "own personal taste", and what the team enjoys.She noted that she didn't think the studio would bow to pressure from fans to do more of the same, but instead be guided by what it thinks is best for itself, and for the series. "I've seen too many TV indicates and books be swayed trying to please a lot of people, and in the process you end up losing the heart of what's there," she noted.

We know that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is "not the end" of the franchise, and it seems that whatever happens next, it'll have at least a little bit of Svedberg-Yen's creativity instilled in it. I wish her the best for whatever her next step is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pedro Pascal says that the character he plays in Behemoth!, his first leading film role, is the “closest thing to me that I’ve ever done.” And because of this, “the experience on set felt surreal in a sort of physically tangible way,” Pascal told the audience during a Q&A at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday.

Directed by Tony Gilroy, Behemoth! tells the story of Alex, a prodigal cellist who returns to Los Angeles and the world of Hollywood film scoring after decades performing symphonic work around the country.

It has been revealed that “The mixing of my own life and this person's life, I've lived a very nomadic one. Don't ask me where home is. And so that felt like it was crossing personal lines for me in a way,” he continued during a post-screening discussion about the film, which featured Pascal and writer-director Tony Gilroy, moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross.

But according to Gilroy, their collaboration on the film almost didn't happen, thanks to an alleged missed connection at a Star Wars event.

Tony Gilroy and Pedro Pascal  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026.

Industry observers note that “We went to a Star Wars convention in Tokyo where we took Andor,” recalled Gilroy. “There was this big Disney dinner so all the Star Wars people are there and [Pascal] was kind of busy and flighty.”.

“I had the flu! I flew from London to Tokyo!” Pascal countered.

According to recent reports, gilroy continued: “He seemed like he was so hip that he didn't come to the dinner. I thought, 'Oh he's got such a great thing going on he's going to some better party; he's not going to a boring dinner.'”.

As the audience laughed, Pascal was quick to set the record straight: “I cannot believe that you thought that I ditched that dinner. I was doing re-shoots of Fantastic Four!” he said. “They flew me to Tokyo that night and flew me back and I was on a set. [Turns toward the audience] Can you believe this?”.

Industry observers note that “Oh my God. I'm calling Kathy Kennedy [the President of Lucasfilm] right away,” Gilroy joked.

Luckily, the moviemaking stars (and schedules) aligned and the pair was able to make their personal, moving film with Pascal serving as Gilroy's “exclamation point. He has all the sadness and all the covering that this character needs to have and the nomadic life.”.

Pedro Pascal, Tony Gilroy and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026.

Pascal and Gilroy formed a genuine bond and are very comfortable making playful jabs at each other, keeping things light but also expressing their gratitude for being able to make Behemoth! their way, in Los Angeles, where the film and television industry has been struggling to regain a foothold. Despite the challenges, past and present, they are holding out hope for human-made storytelling to foster further human connection.

“People's natural resistance to the robot takeover is clear,” stated Gilroy when asked about the rise of AI. “I don't know what's going to happen. I really don't. The music scene out here is the coral reef of what's happened. It's been dying out here for the last 15 years… It's grooving a little bit now. I think people want humans. I don't know what's going to come back, but this is this incredibly humanizing element of movies that's happened. Can it be replaced by AI? Probably, quite shockingly, simply. There's probably an emotional amplitude knob on some f—ing algorithm, but this movie is organic.”.

Pedro Pascal and Tony Gilroy  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that pascal walked away from Behemoth! feeling optimistic. “The experience of shooting this movie definitely injected me with a tremendous amount of hope,” he said. “We weren't making money on this movie. Nobody was. And you had the most expensive people involved in this film because of their talent and their experience. So there was just this purity of love in the work from every single department, and that was incredibly contagious. And it was primarily locations, and so Los Angeles was just constantly revealing itself in all of these magical ways because we were so location-based. I had shot a series in Colombia for three seasons, and I would argue that the primary character of that series, Narcos, was shooting it in the country of Colombia because there was only one way of capturing that energy and that physical story. And LA did that as well. And then it's so tender. I think the story is incredibly tender. Would you ever expect it from this guy [gestures to Gilroy]?”.

Recent findings suggest that “Oh my God. What a cold, weird thing to say,” the director joked.

“There are other movies this year that I think in their own way, movies that I've seen this year that I love so much, that fight for humanity and the storytelling,” Pascal continued. “So I think that there is a sort of pushback that could be really, really thrilling as far as [creativity] is concerned, as far as politics is concerned. We want to be human beings and we want to be connected to one another and we want to tell each other's stories and witness each other's stories and we want to look after each other and all that shit. That's my hope.”.

Tony Gilroy at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026.

Gilroy had another suggestion: “Blow up the AI centers, man," he joked. “I don't mean to blow them up. I mean blow them up at the voting box. Go and vote and blow them up. Go see the Musk documentary, man. Go see that, watch the whole four hours. I'm pitching my movie [here], but watch that movie.”.

The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that well, whaddaya know? Turns out all you need to make a great videogame is around a decade of time, the GDP of a BRICS nation, and a marketing machine pervasive to the point of totalitarianism. The reviews for Grand Theft Auto 6—Rockstar's sequel to that game that would splash "GOURANGA!" on the screen when you ran over enough people—are in. People like it a lot.

No, really, they're out of their gourd for this one, folks. GTA 6 might just be the most absurdly hyped game in history, and yet the mad lads at Rockstar really seem to have pulled it off. Of course, the game's true test—its review on PC Gamer dot com and its accompanying magazine—hasn't happened yet. We'll have to wait for the all-but-certain PC port for that. For now, you can read our impressions of the console version here.

But our console brethren have been putting pen to paper to get their thoughts down, and the reviews for GTA 6 are flowing thick and fast. Here's a sample platter of them, to give you an idea of just how nuts people are going for this thing.

GameSpot's Tamoor Hussain paints a picture of Leonida that overflows with detail, calling it "a game of staggering scope and scale obsessed with small details that could be lost in its vastness, a giant haystack full of needles that you’ll constantly find, creating delight in their improbable discovery". I get the impression that a year from now, five years, ten years, there will still be people rushing to subreddits and forums (if we still have those) to ask if others have seen this or that little detail Rockstar tucked into some obscure corner of its humungous world.

A second perfect score from the gang at IGN, whose Luke Reilly had a great time doing things like:.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Most of which you could feasibly cram into a game whose goal was to simulate my dad, but in GTA 6 it all forms part of a world that constantly surprises you with things to do. "I see no real limit to the amount of time I could spend here, endlessly exploring and interacting with Vice City and the massive area surrounding it", writes Reilly, adding that—despite having beaten the game with 120 hours of playtime under his belt—"While the well-paced story effectively nudged me around the map, there are still vast sections of it that I’m yet to even visit".

Sources indicate that our brothers in arms at GR note that GTA 6 is an improvement on every entry in the series before it: "there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments", writes Josh West, who calls the game (affectionately) "the ultimate time vampire" where "every one of your actions ultimately impacts the lives of Jason and Lucia". Honestly, sounds like a nerve-wracking amount of responsibility for me.

The Newly introduced York Times – Too stately to give a review score but it's an "NYT Critic’s Pick".

According to recent reports, you know a videogame has broken containment when the grey lady is getting in on the review beat. The NYT's Yussef Cole zeroed in on GTA 6's heart in his review: the relationship between protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos—"This is a game about love and relationships, their joy and heartache, and the work required to make them successful", he writes, noting that players can choose to hold hands with their paramour at the touch of a button. We've come a little ways from beating people to death with dildos, folks (though you may well still be able to do that; I'd be surprised if you couldn't).

Giant Bomb (shoutout to Charlie Tunoku) joins in with the hosannahs for GTA 6, describing it as one of those games that feels like a step up for the medium as a whole. "Grand Theft Auto VI is Rockstar’s best game", writes Dan Ryckert. "In the thirteen years between entries of one of the biggest franchises in entertainment, fans’ expectations grew to a level that felt unrealistic. Somehow, Rockstar has managed to overdeliver on the most hyped video game of all time".

In a recent development, the Guardian's Keza MacDonald writes that Rockstar's Leonida is so realistic as to defy belief, but that in its humid, gator-ridden byways you will find scope for both "foulmouthed, OTT chaos—as well as fresh empathy for the fugitive couple at its centre". It is a game, it seems, that is almost too big and varied to squeeze into something like a regular review. "it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it’s hard to know where to start". But you bet those experiences are many, varied, and shockingly fleshed-out.

Bloomberg – Unscored, but you get the picture.

Sources indicate that bloomberg's Jason Schreier, who you may recognise from videogame scoops, is in love with GTA 6 too. He opens with a description of one of the random events that can happen to players in the game, in which he witnessed a crash and found himself enlisted into an NPC's scam to sue a parody of Amazon for millions. "Incidents like this, elaborate depictions of a heightened reality, happen constantly in Grand Theft Auto 6", he writes. "The joy of Grand Theft Auto VI, much like The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Elden Ring before it, comes from discovering its world’s delights and seeing how it reacts to your actions".

It perhaps tells us something that the only non-perfect score on this list is… a 4.5/5 overflowing with praise. Slant's Justin Clark calls GTA 6 "something above and beyond anything the AAA gaming space has ever produced", and has oodles of praise for its rich and hyper-detailed open world. He also thinks that, you know, what's an open world compared to the "first truly meaningful interactive relationship between two semi-realistic grown-ass adults in the entire medium", which Rockstar has also managed to pull off here. "Home, for Jason and Lucia, is each other. Whether there’s $2 million or $2 in their bank accounts, and whether they got it from an honest job or by decimating a metropolitan police force with a grenade launcher, letting these two make a home in each other is the only investment that truly matters—and the best one Rockstar could have ever made, creatively.".

One of Josh's first memories is of playing Quake 2 on the family computer when he was much too young to be doing that, and he's been irreparably game-brained ever since. His writing has been featured in Vice, Fanbyte, and the Financial Times. He'll play pretty much anything, and has written far too much on everything from visual novels to Assassin's Creed. His most profound loves are for CRPGs, immersive sims, and any game whose ambition outstrips its budget. He thinks you're all far too mean about Deus Ex: Invisible War.

Rockstar Games has packed GTA 6 with more detail than any of its previous games, including some truly impressive animations.

Recent findings suggest that let’s start with one of the earliest animations I spotted that truly made me go “Whhhooooaaa…” I parked too close to a car, and Jason was unable to fully open his door. Jason and Lucia might be murderers who rob and steal, but they aren’t litterbugs!

It has been revealed that one animation that really caught me off-guard happened when I was testing how much damage cars in GTA 6 can take before they stop working. I found an empty parking lot, lined up my car with a nearby wall, and floored the accelerator. I expected to slam into the wall and total the front of my vehicle. Instead….

In a recent development, again, GTA 6 has so many surprising animations and details. I can’t list them all here because I know I’ve not found them all yet. Maybe I never will? Breaking: Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - founded by ex-GTA veteran - has a mountain of debt, and the main initiative for paying it back is litigation

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Beleaguered Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - the manufacturer created by former Rockstar and Grand Theft Auto producer Leslie Benzies - apparently owes approximately £62 million in debt. And a huge chunk of that appears to be owed to Chinese gaming company NetEase (£36.5m), though more than £1m appears to be owed to Benzies himself.

This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back. And the organization's "largest" potential asset, according to the administrators, is litigation.

According to recent reports, "Prior to the Manufacturer's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary.

"The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that any such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions.".

In a recent development, this tallies with the narrative spun by co-tech giant leader Mark Gerhard as the company waded into deep water. Gerhard blamed "organised espionage and corporate sabotage" for the studio's difficulties as multiple rounds of layoffs shredded Build a Rocket Boy. "People had their hands on the scale and deliberately tried to shape a negative narrative around the product," Gerhard mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that the situation he's referring to is likely the alleged smear campaign made against the game, which Gerhand reportedly claimed in an internal meeting this year was paid for by a "big American tech giant" and then run by a UK company called Ritual Network, which apparently had influencers, journalists and staff at Build a Rocket Boy deliberately sabotage the game's release. That's according to an account of a videoed internal meeting reportedly seen by Insider Gaming earlier this year.

It had nothing to do with the dire state of Mindseye when it rolled out, then. Eurogamer awarded it one out of five stars, chastising its "ridiculous story, inconsistent writing, poorly designed mission scenarios, and utterly atrocious combat" in our Mindseye review.

In a recent development, build a Rocket Boy was founded in 2016, and its first game, Everywhere - a sort of online gaming platform - was announced in 2022. It never materialised, but a part of that vision was carved out to become a standalone game experience of its own along the way, and that's how we got Mindseye - a take on a Grand Theft Auto formula. Whether or not the litigation is successful and can recoup any of Build a Rocket Boy's debts remains to be seen, but there's a financial mountain for the studio to climb if it hopes to operate again.

Back in August, the public was devastated to learn that actress Hayden Panettiere died at age 36. This was a huge shock, especially considering her brother died just a few years earlier. Fans are still mourning and re-watching her work on projects like Heroes, and plenty of people were surprised when Panettiere's mother Lesley Vogel didn't attend her celebration of life back in September. Now Vogel is speaking out and explaining her absence for the services.

It has been revealed that fans still have questions about Hayden Panettiere's death, and were curious about why her mother wasn't in attendance for the late actress' funeral services. Lesley Vogel recently appeared on Inside Edition, where she explained why she chose to opt out of her daughter's celebration of life. She was quoted saying:.

I just didn’t want to rock the boat either; it was probably for the best.

During the interview, she shared that she and Hayden Panettiere drifted away from each other after the Scream actress' relationship with ex Brian Hickerson started picking up. They mother and daughter seemingly had a difficult relationship, some of which was mentioned in the actress' memoir This Is Me: A Reckoning. Still, it was surprising for some that Vogel didn't attend the funeral services.

While appearing in the same interview, Lesley Vogel claimed that she was indeed invited, but didn't think her presence would be helpful during this difficult time. She went on to say:.

I knew that some of the people there wanted to believe I was the horrible mother because Hayden was angry and made statements.

Industry observers note that clearly this was a complicated situation, which might explain why Hayden Panettiere's mother ultimately decided not to attend her funeral. She knew there'd be discourse about her either way, but is seemingly at peace with her decision. Inside Edition contacted Brian Hickerson for a comment, but did not hear back from him.

Sources indicate that panettiere's death hit the public hard, largely because she grew up right in front of our eyes, including early roles in projects like Remember the Titans and A Bug's Life. Millennial fans in particular grew up alongside her, and there was a ton of love her work on Ice Princess, Heroes, Nashville, and the Scream movies (the latter of which are streaming with a Paramount+ subscription). Folks were thrilled when she reprised her role as Kirby Reed in Scream VI, with Panettiere thanking fans who "came to her rescue". Clearly she's someone who meant a great deal to her fans, many of whom are still processing her death. As for Lesley Vogel, she's given an explanation for missing her late daughter's funeral.

Hayden Panettiere's legacy lives on through her various acting credits. Heroes is streaming on Netflix, while Nashville is over on Pluto TV. Our thoughts continue to be with her loved ones as they mourn and grapple with the loss.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in unexpected news, Kensington Palace has just declared that Kate Middleton will accompany Prince William on his upcoming three-day official visit to Mumbai, India. The trip, which commences on Monday, will mark their first joint tour outside the United Kingdom in the past four years and represents a newly introduced milestone in Kate Middleton’s gradual return to public duties since she was diagnosed with cancer in early 2024 and began scaling back her official engagements.

Last May, the princess made a brief solo trip to Italy to learn about early childhood development, but this trip to India (a nine-hour flight from London) represents her first long-distance journey and her highest-profile diplomatic engagement since the Caribbean tour she undertook in 2022 and the Earthshot Awards gala she attended in Boston that same year.

"So proud, I'm very, very proud. She's been amazing. She's been through so much in the last couple of years, particularly," William shared on UK radio show Heart Breakfast in May, pleased to see that Kate was “gradually resuming” her travels. Still, the heir to the throne wanted to be cautious and warned that these visits are very taxing. "Away trips like that take a lot out of you," he explained. "So we have to balance that, make sure she's, she's OK and rested, but she's in good form.".

The royal couple at the 2022 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Boston, their most recent joint trip abroad to date.

The reason for the visit is the sixth edition of the Earthshot Prize, an initiative spearheaded by the heir to the British throne that each year awards one million pounds (about $1,323,249) to five innovative environmental projects and which, after making stops in other cities abroad such as Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro, is now taking place in the country that has produced the most finalists and winners in the competition’s history.

It has been revealed that standout finalists this year include Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, for its fleet of electric motorcycle taxis designed to reduce urban pollution, and Mahila Housing Trust, which installs reflective roofs capable of lowering the temperature inside homes by up to five degrees during extreme heat. The awards ceremony will be held this Tuesday evening at the Jio World Centre in Mumbai and will feature a performance by the band Take That and be attended by celebrities such as actor Rami Malek.

William and Kate during their 2016 visit to the Taj Mahal.

It has been revealed that hours before the main event, the Prince and Princess of Wales will also preside over the first edition of the Earthshot Children’s Awards, a competition in which 15,000 schools from 24 Indian states have participated with environmental proposals designed by young people aged 9 to 17. The itinerary also includes a solo appearance by Kate Middleton, meetings with the Bollywood film industry, cricket-related celebrations, and a possible meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

In addition to being a positive sign regarding the princess’s health, this return to India holds strong symbolic significance for the couple, who last visited the country in April 2016. On that occasion, the then-Duke and Duchess of Cambridge visited the Taj Mahal and posed on the same white marble bench where Princess Diana was photographed alone in 1992—an image that has gone down in history as a reflection of the breakdown of her marriage to the now-King Charles III.

Originally published by Vanity Fair Spain.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anne Hathaway has millions of fans thanks to her expansive acting catalog, but her husband, Adam Shulman, has always felt like home.

“I knew from the second I met him that he was the love of my life,” Hathaway told Harper’s Bazaar UK in February 2013, less than one year after they got married.

Sources indicate that the Princess Diaries star recalled telling a mutual friend of theirs, “I’m going to marry that man,” soon after they first crossed paths. “I think he thought I was a little nuts, which I am a bit, but I’m also nice,” she teased.

Hathaway — who declared in June 2026 that she is expecting her third baby with Shulman — isn’t the only one who is happy she met her match in the jewelry designer.

Her Devil Wears Prada 2 costar Emily Blunt told Elle in March 2017 that Shulman “has been Annie’s greatest achievement in many ways. He’s sort of home away from the storm of fame that she lives with.”.

Sources indicate that blunt gushed, “Being with the right person has been a major part of her growth, but I don’t think she cares as much anymore. That’s something both of us feel now: Who f***ing cares? You get to a point where the stuff that you used to sweat just doesn’t matter. It’s a great place to be.”.

Scroll down to learn more about Hathaway’s husband:.

Sources indicate that after growing up in New York, Shulman attended Brown University. He graduated in 2003 with a bachelor’s of arts in theater.

In a recent development, shulman is a man of many talents, one of which is working as a jewelry designer. His brand is called James Banks Design, which according to its website makes handmade pieces from recycled materials in Southern California.

Industry News: Infinity Nikki fans threaten to boycott game after promotion by Elon Musk's mother, but there may be a genuine reason for her involvement

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (499 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, cozy, open-world dress-up game, is at the centre of controversy again, though this time not because fans disliked one of the game's updates.
  • Some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk.
  • While some fans are worried Tesla's cars may be coming to the game, many also simply don't want their game associated with Elon Musk and his family.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, cozy, open-world dress-up game, is at the centre of controversy again, though this time not because fans disliked one of the game's updates. Instead, it's because of… Elon Musk's mother.

Some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk. The trailer is for a new update - dubbed Cicia - which adds the ability to drive futuristic hovering cars. The reveal comes days after a widely mocked demonstration of Musk's own Tesla "flying car", which doesn't actually fly.

While some fans are worried Tesla's cars may be coming to the game, many also simply don't want their game associated with Elon Musk and his family.

"If they promote Tesla or mention him in the game I'm 100 percent dropping it," wrote one Reddit user (via The Gamer). "Why would they involve that man in a girly fashion game, and if they wanted a car brand partnership why not a Chinese one??!? Infold is addicted to negative attention I swear.".

"If Tesla is somehow involved in the design of the car (or worse, an in-game promotion), then I might have to let go," wrote another person in the same thread. "Please please please be wrong.".

It has been revealed that though Maye Musk's involvement might seem random, there may be a good explanation for it. "Here's something that might surprise people who only know her as Elon's mother: Maye Musk is a celebrity in China in her own right," Reddit user BarbieSpeedRacer explained.

Recent findings suggest that "She's a successful model, an author, and a recognisable advertising personality. Her memoir became popular with Chinese readers, and she's appeared in campaigns and promotional events for brands including OPPO, Fila, and JNBY.".

Her image as "a woman in her seventies who continues to work as a fashion model" is one that resonates with the game's Chinese audience, apparently, especially "among women interested in fashion, beauty, and lifestyle content".

"A Chinese organization makes an advertisement featuring a celebrity popular in China, and an international fandom interprets that decision almost exclusively through the lens of American domestic politics," the post added.

Sources indicate that so far, calls for a boycott don't appear to have coalesced into a movement, at least judging by the game's subreddit. Even if Western players were to organise one, it's not likely to hurt Infinity Nikki much, as most of the game's revenue - estimated at more than 80 percent - comes from Chinese players.

In Eurogamer's Infinity Nikki review, Jessica Orr said it advances the genre of open-world gacha games and brings competition to rival developer miHoYo, writing: "The changes in length, combat and progression all feel utterly invigorating compared to other Genshin-likes, and it's why Infinity Nikki feels like it could (and should) be on the same trajectory to shake up the gacha scene just like Genshin Impact did in 2020.".

The latest sales data for GTA 6 pre-purchases show that the game has passed 16 million units sold worldwide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that AMD landed itself in hot water with gamers a couple of weeks back by saying the quiet part out loud: CEO Dr. Lisa Su announced that it was a "datacentre-first organization" in a call with investors, who were likely to want to hear that sorta thing. Yet upon reaching gamers' ears, the news wasn't so well received.

Now, AMD Japan has tried to settle things down by proclaiming "AMD loves gamers.".

To be fair, those two statements aren't mutually exclusive. AMD can be datacentre first, and absolutely is, and still claim to care about gaming. Though when supply for key components is tight and prices are rising, we're definitely looking for a little more than kind words at this time.

What makes matters worse is that AMD Japan also added: "AMD values its interactions with gamers above all else.".

Now, that's a much tougher sell.

In a recent development, in Q3, AMD made more than double the cash from its datacentre segment ($8.5 billion) than its client and gaming segment ($3.7 billion)—the latter includes various Ryzen, as well as Radeon, products. Pure gaming revenue was a mere $773 million, and dropping fast, whereas datacentre revenue was up 97%.

It has been revealed that so, from a purely business perspective, AMD is undoubtedly all in on datacentres. I don't like to admit it, but it makes sense for a company owned by shareholders to go after the biggest growth market. But all the more reason not to claim an undying love for gamers—it just doesn't pass muster.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

In a recent development, AMD Japan is responding to a tweet from our sister site, Tom's Hardware, who had reported that the company's CEO had attended a store opening for a latest Micro Center in Austin, Texas and was handing out autographed graphics cards and swag bags to lucky attendees. So, in that sense, AMD can claim to have helped a handful of gamers directly. An RX 9070 XT signed by Lisa Su may hold its value more than one signed by Jensen Huang.

Nevertheless, the post on X hasn't been too well received. A reader note has been added to note AMD's claim to be a datacentre first tech giant, and the replies are a bit of a dumpster fire.

Recent findings suggest that truth be told, it's not a good time to claim to care about the gamers, whether there's any truth to the claim or not. From graphics cards to SSDs, we're stuck with extremely high prices, beyond most reasonable budgets, and few exciting product debuts to note—except monitors. Thank God for monitors.

As Johnny Depp Faces Pirates Of The Caribbean 6 Rumors, Another Star Weighs In On Returning

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (806 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Johnny Depp returning to theaters in Ebenezer on the 2026 movie schedule, renewed interest has grown in whether he'll ever play Captain Jack Sparrow again.
  • Mackenzie Crook, who played the perpetually confused Ragetti in the first three Pirates movies, recently discussed the possibility of returning to the franchise during an appearance on The Daily Beast's Obsessed podcast.
  • It has been revealed that yes, I think I would for the hell of it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Johnny Depp returning to theaters in Ebenezer on the 2026 movie schedule, renewed interest has grown in whether he'll ever play Captain Jack Sparrow again. Producer Jerry Bruckheimer has already confirmed that discussions have taken place about bringing Depp back for Pirates of the Caribbean 6, although nothing has been officially declared. Now another familiar face from the original movies has weighed in, and I have to admit, this is one reunion I'd love to see happen.

Mackenzie Crook, who played the perpetually confused Ragetti in the first three Pirates movies, recently discussed the possibility of returning to the franchise during an appearance on The Daily Beast's Obsessed podcast. The actor, who starred alongside Lee Arenberg's Pintel as one of the series' most entertaining comedic duos, hasn't appeared in a Pirates movie since 2007's At World's End. Although nearly 20 years later, he sounds more than willing to dig out that wooden eye. Crook explained:.

It has been revealed that yes, I think I would for the hell of it. It would be so interesting – obviously it would depend on the script – to even just have a cameo to see what happened to those characters, Pintel and Ragetti, what happened to them after we last saw them. Again, I was really fond of those characters and working with Lee Arenberg, who plays Pintel. Yeah, we had a blast doing that stuff. It was great.

Sources indicate that I would absolutely love this. Pintel and Ragetti were two of my favorite supporting characters from the original trilogy, and their ridiculous behavior provided some great comic relief between all the sword fights and increasingly more extravagant set pieces.

For anybody who needs a refresher, the pair started as members of Barbossa's cursed crew in The Curse of the Black Pearl. Ragetti was the skinny, somewhat dimwitted pirate with a wooden eye. Pintel was his considerably louder and equally incompetent partner.

Recent findings suggest that somehow, they survived three movies filled with undead pirates, sea monsters and increasingly complicated betrayals. That's honestly impressive considering how frequently they seemed to have no idea what was going on. While I certainly want to see Johnny Depp return as Jack Sparrow, I think bringing back characters like these could be just as important to making another Pirates movie feel connected to the originals.

Crook also had some interesting memories of working on the films. During the interview, he recalled the sometimes exhausting experience of shooting aboard actual ships at sea. He also discussed the rather uncomfortable process of bringing Ragetti's wooden eye to life, which required wearing two contact lenses, including one designed to create the appearance of wood grain.

Industry observers note that apparently, playing a pirate wasn't quite as glamorous as it looked. The actor also reflected on the amount of practical filmmaking involved in the original trilogy. Although the movies relied heavily on visual effects, Crook remembered productions where crews actually rigged ships with explosives rather than recreating everything digitally. He described those experiences as some of the last examples of old-fashioned blockbuster filmmaking.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Sources indicate that I think that's part of what makes those first three movies so much fun to revisit with a Disney+ subscription. Even when the stories got complicated, something fantastically chaotic about watching these characters run around enormous pirate ships, usually making whatever situation they were in considerably worse. Of course, whether any of them actually return is another matter.

Bruckheimer previously confirmed that he's been speaking with Depp about a sixth movie, although the project remains in development. Depp recently suggested he'd be interested in helping give the franchise a proper sendoff, particularly if it meant working with Bruckheimer again.

Meanwhile, other original cast members have expressed interest in returning. Orlando Bloom has discussed the possibility of another Pirates movie, though there's still no indication that Will Turner will be part of whatever Disney ultimately decides to make.

That's really where we stand. There's no confirmed cast or release date for Pirates of the Caribbean 6, and Crook's comments are just an expression of interest, not evidence he's been approached.

I do like his idea of a cameo that lets audiences catch up with Pintel and Ragetti. It's been almost two decades since we last saw the two idiots, and I can't help wondering what they've been doing with themselves.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft recently hired games industry veteran Christoph Hartmann to become the general manager of Creative House 2, which is now known as Massive Entertainment.
  • Sources indicate that ubisoft recently hired games industry veteran Christoph Hartmann to become the general manager of Creative House 2, which is now known as Massive Entertainment.
  • He told Variety that what he means by this is that Massive can be like A24 in that it can make games that are both critically and commercially successful.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft recently hired games industry veteran Christoph Hartmann to become the general manager of Creative House 2, which is now known as Massive Entertainment. In a fresh interview, Hartmann talked about his hopes for the unit, saying his dream would be for it to become "like the A24 of video games." He told Variety that what he means by this is that Massive can be like A24 in that it can make games that are both critically and commercially successful. A24's biggest hit ever was this year's Backrooms, which made more than $400 million worldwide against a reported budget of $10 million and was received positively by fans and critics. Some of A24's other recent major critical and commercial hits have included Marty Supreme ($192 million), Everything Everywhere All at Once ($148 million), The Drama ($135 million), and Civil War ($127 million). Jesse Plemons in A24's Civil War. Saying Ubisoft's Massive could aim for what A24 is doing is certainly an ambitious goal, and it's not the first time that Hartmann has made such a bold claim about what he's working on. When he was at Amazon, Hartmann said his objective was to help Amazon become “the Disney of the future,” with gaming standing alongside TV, film, music, and retail. Massive covers franchises like The Division, Ghost Recon, Splinter Cell, and March of Giants (which Ubisoft bought from Hartmann's previous organization, Amazon). "Hartmann’s role is to oversee strategic direction and development of the studios and brands under Creative House 2 [now Massive]," Ubisoft said. Hartmann told Variety that he wants Massive to "definitely not" be a place that only makes shooter games. "I want us to be a label which really looks after the core gamer. And what I mean by that, it’s almost easier to describe what we’re not going to do. So I’m not going to do a racing game. I’m not going to do sports. I’m not going to do a casual kids title. But could we do an RPG one day? Could we do MMO? Could I maybe do even a strategy game? Sure, it’s all coming down to the right talent," he said. Hartmann also discussed why he left Amazon, saying the company is focused on the AI buildout right now and "games just can't be their prime focus right now." Prior to Amazon, Hartmann worked at 2K for decades. Ubisoft restructured its business around the Creative House model after taking investment from Tencent to secure the company's financial future. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial, the director follows the rise of OpenAI and a few of its pioneers: Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever and Mira Murati. The result is one of the most talked-about and timely films of the season.

“The topic is not the artificial intelligence for me, but it's the people who imagined it, who created it, who exploited it and who are still in the mix of doing all these things,” Guadagnino said during a discussion led by VF's Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci, at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday. “I was very much into trying to decipher, understand this world of this fresh generation, let’s say tech bros, that were somehow behaving in a way that was not exactly as you could see the previous generation doing … So it was too attractive not to try to meet these people in the eyes and too attractive not to do so with this incredible group of performers who were going to go and jump the cliff of this.”.

Luca Guadagnino and Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026.

According to recent reports, guadagnino was joined by cast members Andrew Garfield (who plays Altman), Yura Borisov (who plays Sutskever) and Monica Barbaro (who plays Murati) for a post-screening conversation. The actors were challenged with preparing to play real people who they were not able to interact with ahead of time, instead relying on interviews, video recordings, and other research in order to get into their characters.

Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026.

Industry observers note that “[Sam Altman] still is unknowable to me and I'm fascinated by him continuously and exponentially, for here until eternity," Garfield remarked about OpenAI's co-founder and CEO. “And it's key to try to understand because as Luca said, these are the kids that have the reins of the future and we've somehow allowed them to just hold onto them. And we've kind of given our autonomy over or it's been taken from behind our backs.”.

He added: “It's a remarkable thing to have the resilience to go and sleep every night, knowing that you're really doing a lot of damage.”.

Sources indicate that barbaro remarked the fact that Murati is very private helped her understand the former OpenAI CTO. “That is indicative of a kind of behavior and personality type and it pointed me in a certain direction as far as her values were concerned,” she said. “And we also had a lot of wonderful consultants, people who worked with them at OpenAI, but who were no longer with the tech giant, kind of telling us what jokes and things that they would make.”.

Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026.

According to recent reports, for Borisov, he hopes his portrayal does Sutskever justice and that people will want to know or understand him more. “I started to watch videos about him and looked at his social media, trying just to understand what he's talking about in his interviews,” the actor explained. "And step by step, as much as I discovered him, it was more and more scary for me because I started to respect and love him more and more.".

Monica Barbaro, Andrew Garfield and Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026.

The conversation had its own meta moment of sorts, when Barbaro posed a question to Guiducci about his decision to profile and feature Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair’s New Establishment Issue.

"You faced heat for presenting, maybe some people would say pedestalizing Sam Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair, what is your take on that?" Barbaro asked.

“I think that the magazine is an arena where these things have to play out,” Guiducci stated. “It's so interesting to me to...have the [forthcoming] feature about this film in the matter that was preceded by one where I got to ask Sam about it." Guiducci continued: "Something about [taking Sam's] picture makes people feel, ‘Oh, that's the trophy.’ But photojournalism is journalism too. And I want people to be able to look back at the magazine and see a document of the time that we lived in," he said. "And also, if the photo is what helps me get the interview where we get to know more about these people, I'm going to take it.”.

Monica Barbaro at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026.

Sources indicate that other panel highlights included the subject of ChatGPT, which only Guadagnino admitted to using occasionally to ask about what’s ok to feed his dogs. He also addressed parting ways with the film's original studio partner Amazon and the fortuitous partnership that emerged with fresh distributor NEON.

“I think there is some kind of honor in the decision because they could have written off the movie and that's it,” he stated about Amazon dropping the film from their slate. “And then they allowed us to find a partner and we found the best partner possible… They really believed in the movie.”.

Recent findings suggest that “They really made everything to get us to make the best movie we could,” he continued. "I only have good feelings toward my friends at Amazon. And in a strange way, I kind of understand the decision. Conflict of interest is a substantial thing.”.

Luca Guadagnino at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026.

It has been revealed that the inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

Breaking: You cannot replay missions in GTA 6, but you can use multiple save files, as Rockstar explains how it made missions "harder to fail"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (534 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them.
  • You can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress.
  • It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them. This might be a shock to some people, since the option to do so was included in Rockstar games as recently as GTA 5, but here once you've made progress in the story, that's it. Our reviewer confirmed this in his 100+ hour playthrough of the title.

You can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress. By my maths, that means you're going to want to make a fresh manual save for every 6.6 percent of the game you complete. There is, of course, an auto-save slot, too, that should help you out if you get Busted or Wasted. There will also be key story missions - you will be able to tell when they are, much like you could tell when there was about to be a significant heist in GTA 5, a showdown in GTA: San Andreas, or a raid on a gang lord's mansion in GTA: Vice City - that you may want to save before attempting.

It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6. "The team embraced more of an open-ended design philosophy on this project," states David Hynd, vice president of technology on GTA 6. "For example, we really wanted to reduce the number of Mission fails for the player experimenting or trying something different. And we wanted to encourage the player to do what felt right to them for their particular play style.".

Sources indicate that that means that Rockstar, by considering its deployment of standard gameplay mechanics and enemy AI, and re-evaluating how it approached mission and level design, has created "many different ways" for you to approach any given mission in the game. The result? "It's a lot harder to keep Missions as open as possible (especially in a game as large as this), but the freedom and flexibility it allows the player was worth it," says Hynd. He also notes that the team expects players to "learn and reapply" consistent rules in terms of how the world works - and be surprised when they do and don't apply.

In the previous game, you could access any previous mission you'd completed and be able to play it again on a whim. For GTA 5, you'd simply boot up Story Mode, open the pause menu, go to Game > Replay Mission, and pick the mission you want to play. GTA 6's structure is more complicated, though, hence why Rockstar made the decision to make progress this linear.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 comes out tomorrow. You can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 at the link, and read our 5-star review of the game here. If you want to, ahem, 'travel to Fresh Zealand' to get ahead of the timezones, it seems the country would be happy to have you.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has a lot of details and depth, including dozens of different bird species for people to find. If you're a birder, you're in for a good time. According to The Guardian, Rockstar confirmed that there are 62 types of birds that players can spot. Players can whip out binoculars to "study" birds and animals like they could in Rockstar's last game, Red Dead Redemption II. GTA 6 is almost here. As PC Gamer reminds us, Florida is home to more than 500 bird types, so GTA 6 will have just a fraction of the different kinds of birds people can find in real Florida. GTA 6 was never going to replicate every single bird, of course. Some of the birds that are found in Florida, and probably GTA 6 as well, include flamingoes, spoonbills, wood storks, egrets, kites, terns, and scrub jays. Florida is also home to bald eagles, and we'd expect them to show up in GTA 6. Inclusive of birds, GTA 6 has more than 170 animal types, including cane toads, alligators, manatees, and rhesus macaque monkeys. GTA 6 debuts on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game launches at midnight local time, so it will be playable for people in New Zealand and Australia very soon. You can switch your Xbox region to New Zealand to play early, if that works. I make a beeline for Paris Hilton to thank her for the facial I received at her spa this week, while Dancing With the Stars alums Rumer and Jenna Dewan immediately pull out their phones to compare pictures of their kids.

Industry observers note that then I spot Sofia Richie Grainge and her husband, Atlantic Records CEO Elliot Grainge. I snake through throngs of elegant people and poke Elliot’s back twice. “Elliot, it’s Tallulah! We went to Wildwood together!” He instantly remembers me. “Tallulah was the cool girl in class,” he tells Sofia. I blush, but don’t feel the need to correct him.

Scout approaches and says, almost incredulously, “Hi, I’m Scout…you guys just signed me at Atlantic Records.” Elliot grabs her shoulders. “We’re so happy to have you. Are you happy with us?” She can’t say “yes” fast enough.

In a recent development, the program begins with Keke Palmer, who completely owns the stage, telling hilarious stories about her son before shifting into heartfelt candor about the gift of watching him grow. Kerry Washington thanks the sponsors and introduces Baby2Baby’s new permanent headquarters, “a promise to millions of children. Not just for today, but for decades to come.”.

In a recent development, then Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein, the organization’s CEOs, come to the stage, sharing the work—no, the magic—they have created over 15 years. Their first gala in 2012 raised $1 million. Last year’s raised $18 million. To date, they’ve distributed an astonishing 850 million essential items to people in need across all 50 states, responded to over 150 disasters, developed their own diaper production line during COVID, and expanded into mental health support for latest mothers. The mission remains the same, but the scale is impossible to comprehend.

Recent findings suggest that now Rumer, Scout, and I are all crying during a short video about two families impacted by Baby2Baby. The feeling is palpable for the rest of the room.

As the live auction begins, I catch my mom discreetly reading over a printout of her speech. I don’t feel nerves coming off her, but a desire to match the elegance and integrity surrounding us.

Sources indicate that andrew Garfield takes the stage and speaks directly to my mom about the woman he knows. “She is a miracle,” he claims.

Then it’s Demi’s turn. Holding her gleaming award in two hands, she thanks Andrew for carving out time amid his Artificial press tour. My mother adores Andrew, a feeling shared across our family.

Alone on stage in her Carolina gown (sans pockets), she asks everyone to breathe. “Inhale. Exhale.” That breath, she claims, is the relief Baby2Baby provides when a mother no longer has to choose between dinner and diapers. “Your child matters, you matter, and you are not alone.” She leaves us with the idea that the essence of this work is to be remarkably human. Baby to baby, mother to mother, soul to soul.

Then Cardi B takes the stage and the atmosphere shifts with a jolt. Everyone is on their feet dancing. The official after-party begins, but I’m turning back into a pumpkin in towering satin stilettos. It was a remarkably beautiful night, and I’m left with the overwhelming desire to do more—to show up for someone who may not have the ability to show up for themselves or their precious loved ones.

But for this on-scene reporter’s inaugural correspondence, it was ultimately Baby2Baby2Bedtime.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It may be hard to notice what with all the Grand Theft Auto 6-ness happening right now, but the games industry has had a very rough last few years. This isn't to say no great games have come out this year. I've actually had a great time, what with Resident Evil Requiem, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and Substantial Walk—oh and I've heard that Queen's Domain is rather good also.

But the matter of how big studios are able to balance their budget still stands. “Around content, AAA is under the most amount of threat," former Take-Two CEO, Ben Feder claims in an interview with The Game Business. "They’re not big enough to really be platforms on the one hand, and they’re not small enough to really innovate on the other. If you talk to the major publishers, they cannot figure out a way to make a game for less than $300 million, and that to me is just not sustainable.".

Sources indicate that we now know for sure that GTA 6 is a winner: just look at this review score round up. But there are some worried that replicating this success is nigh impossible for any other studio. As Feder puts it, not everyone can take their "entire development team, putting them in a time capsule, burying them in the ground, and five years later they pop out and say, 'Voila, here it is.'" Most studios simply do not have the capacity or funds to have a team solely working on a project for around a decade.

"Three to five years ago, that was reasonable because we know what they’re building, it’s good IP, they have a niche, and we know what the world’s going to look like when they pop out of the ground," Feder adds. "Today, while they’re underground, on the surface of planet Earth all of this change is happening, not just technologically but also with respect to consumer tastes and expectations. They may come out five years from now, and the world may not care.".

Recent findings suggest that feder goes on to explain that GTA 6 is the exception to this rule as it's able to deliver "escape velocity". I take this to mean the ridiculous amounts of hype and money that surround this game is why it's able to retain this old way of working. "Scale matters there, and you need an enormous amount of capital to do that,” Feder says. "The amount of capital required starts with a 'B' not with an 'M', for sure.".

I love our country, and I love Nvidia." Huang acknowledged that he "did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia" and owned up to making "serious mistakes in my personal life." He said he created problems for Nvidia's Board of Directors and he said he "deeply" regrets that. "I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation," he said. https://twitter.com/JensenHuang/status/2122726005219737649 Nvidia was the world's biggest company by market cap until the company's stock price began to crash in October, and it fell further after the controversies came to light, including multiple affairs beyond the one with the alleged spy. To be sure, Nvidia remains a juggernaut--it's at the moment the No. 2 biggest company in the world, with a market cap of $3.75 trillion. Only Apple, with a market cap above $4 trillion, is bigger than Nvidia. The New York Times and other media outlets reported that Huang had a romantic relationship with the former CEO of the AI company Megaspeed, Alice Huang (no relation). US intelligence sources claim that Alice Huang was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, though China officially denies this narrative and says it's an effort by the US to smear China. Megaspeed, for its part, said Alice Huang left the company in 2025 and denied any wrongdoing in the Nvidia scandal. The Nvidia controversies have led to turmoil in the stock market, in part because Nvidia is one of the "Mag 7" companies that are driving growth in the US. Some of the information coming to light suggests that Nvidia's accounting and export control compliance are not buttoned up, and this has fueled further concerns about the growth potential and returns on investment for the AI trade. Numerous other technology and AI stocks have dropped in value significantly since the Nvidia news broke. Nvidia's interim boss is CFO Colette Kress, who is expected to lead Nvidia's earnings call today, November 17. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that we’re only a few days away from the Traitors: New Blood finale, and I’m willing to admit the obvious.
  • Sources indicate that the biggest, loudest and most obvious change we’ve gotten this season has been the casting of non-celebrities.
  • Industry observers note that the biggest problem by a very large margin with Traitors: New Blood is the episode runtimes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we’re only a few days away from the Traitors: New Blood finale, and I’m willing to admit the obvious. This has not been the best season of The Traitors. In fact, you could easily say this has been a below-average season. Fans on social media and those I have talked to in real life seem to all be in agreement on that. There’s a growing consensus that the show needs to change. I think producers are going to listen, though I’m terrified they’re going to misunderstand the why.

Sources indicate that the biggest, loudest and most obvious change we’ve gotten this season has been the casting of non-celebrities. The US version of The Traitors has historically relied on reality television personalities to provide the drama and bring their fanbases. This season, NBC decided to move the property from Peacock to network television and cast it like a more traditional competition show with randoms. It would be easy to just look at that decision and blame all the problems on the newbies, but that’s actually not the right takeaway.

Industry observers note that the biggest problem by a very large margin with Traitors: New Blood is the episode runtimes. The show simply does not work in an hour-long time slot on NBC. In theory, the episodes on Peacock are the same length, as they’re typically between an hour and an hour and ten minutes. Because they’re on streaming, however, that runtime is the actual length of each episode. On network television, an hour-long time slot is actually forty-two minutes or so of real content, which isn’t even close to the amount of time the players need to complete one cycle of the game.

That means every single episode, the editors are making an impossible choice. They can either not include one or more major elements of the show (the breakfast, the mission, the roundtable and the turret), they can completely remove all of the strategy scenes that happen between those major elements, or they can drop most of the confessionals where the players talk directly to the camera and tell us their motivations and theories. There is simply no way to get through all of that in forty-two minutes. So, that has left every episode feeling either incomplete because it didn’t make it through a full cycle of the game, or feeling like a highlight video that simply recaps the basics of what happened.

That format and structure are the problem. The runtime is the problem. It’s not the cast. Even with less confessionals and less screentime, we’ve gotten good content from these players. I’m not saying the Traitors: New Blood cast is better than the cast on Major Brother 14 or Survivor: Heroes vs Villains, but there are some breakout personalities here and plenty of likeable, solid characters who have popped and would have looked even better with more of a chance to talk to the camera.

Victor is an all-time great Traitors character and should be a reality television mainstay moving forward. He’s electric. I’m personally obsessed with Jay and have had probably ten conversations with people trying to figure out his vibe and what’s going on in his head. It’s not just those two standouts either. There are a half dozen or so other players who play hard and are capable of delivering strong confessionals. Joe, Katie, Tomica, Michael and Shane have all had great moments, and when given a chance, secondary characters like Wyatt, Clyde, Abby, Abbey, Kriste, Ben, Morgan and others have delivered too. They’re just not always getting the screentime because, once again, every episode feels like it’s set on 1.5X speed.

Survivor and The Amazing Race have lengthened their episodes in recent years to help develop the characters and let the episodes breathe more. That’s the obvious solution here for The Traitors. It either needs to move to 90 minutes, or it needs to move back to Peacock. What it absolutely does not need to do is give up on casting newbies. The UK and other countries have had fantastic seasons using randoms, and in an ideal world, it would be a delight to watch Peacock/ NBC switch back and forth between a season with reality stars and a season with plumbers, farmers and firefighters.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

According to recent reports, I love The Traitors. It’s one of my favorite indicates on television, and despite the obvious format issues, I still enjoyed the content we got this season. I’d like to see producers listen to the fan frustration and make a change, but those alterations should be exclusively focused on the format and not on casting.

It's almost time for The Game Awards to kick off a night of trailers and appreciation for the 2026 gaming year, but right now, it's time to see who's in the running to earn some well-deserved kudos. The 2026 Game Awards will be livestreamed from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on December 10, and nominees for the best games across several categories have been announced.

Like previous years, the nominees have been chosen by a global jury of media publications and creator outlets--including GameSpot--and were declared through a dedicated livestream.

Sources indicate that leading the nominations is Grand Theft Auto 6 with eight nominations, Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem with six nominations each, and Phantom Blade Zero has earned an impressive five nominations. Big Walk, 007 First Light, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake have also earned plenty of nods, with four nominations each.

Here's a closer look at which games are in the running for several of the biggest prizes at The Game Awards this year.

The best of the best for 2026, the game that excelled across multiple creative and technical fields.

For the game that was built with an outstanding creative vision and executed it through polished direction and design.

Awarded to the game that not only offers the best story of the year, but also delivers its with exceptional storytelling skills.

Video game graphics have come a long way over the years, and this award recognizes the 2026 game that featured incredible artistic design and animation.

Great game visuals also need equally good audio, and this award is for the best music in a game, pulled from its score, original songs and/or a licensed soundtrack.

Sticking with sound, this award goes to the game with the best in-game audio and sound design.

We've also seen the rise of video game thespians in modern gaming, and this award honors the individual for their voice-over acting and performance capture.

Video games are capable of delivering profound messages, and the Games for Impact award is handed out to the one title that gave players a thought-provoking experience.

Live-service games have continued to be a big draw throughout 2026, and the Best Ongoing Game award is handed out to the title that has shown outstanding development of ongoing content for its players.

In recognition of the game and studio that has provided excellent community support and transparency.

The top prize for indie games at The Game Awards, this one is for the smaller, risky projects that found critical acclaim in 2026.

Another big prize for indie developers, Best Indie Debut Game is awarded to the independent studio that produced and shipped its first game in 2026.

Exactly what you expect, this is the award for the best game that's playable on a mobile device.

Likewise, this award goes to the best game that's playable across virtual, mixed or augmented reality, irrespective of platform.

It's all about action with this award, which focuses on the fine art of crafting exhilarating combat.

This prize goes to the game that not only offers polished combat, but also slick traversal and puzzle-solving.

Another genre favorite, the award for Best RPG recognizes the game that gave players rich character customization and progression across their journey, and it also includes nominees for MMORPGs.

There was no shortage of cool fighting games in 2026, and this award will recognize the best brawler of the year.

For the game that was appropriate for family play, irrespective of genre or platform.

The Game Awards will also honor the best simulation and strategy games of the year with this prize.

Given to the best traditional or non-traditional sports and racing game of the year.

Awarded to the game that nails online multiplayer gameplay and design--including co-op and massively multiplayer experiences.

Whether it's a movie, TV series, or podcast adaptation of a video game, the award for Best Adaptation will recognize it for how creatively and authentically the source material is adapted as a piece of entertainment.

It has been revealed that set engines to hype! The award for Most Anticipated Game--which is for a game coming after December 10, 2026--recognizes the upcoming release that has fans excited for the future and how the video game medium could possibly be pushed forward to latest heights.

Alex Michel has kept a low-profile since starring as the very first Bachelor in 2002. After giving his final rose to Amanda Marsh in the finale — and opting not to propose — the pair went their separate ways in 2003 after 10 months of dating. He currently resides in Washington, D.C. and works as a media industry executive. Amanda, who is engaged to her longtime love Chris, told Us exclusively in July 2020 that Alex is married with kids.

According to recent reports, after popping the question to Helene Eksterowicz during the season 2 finale of The Bachelor in 2002, the twosome called it quits weeks after the last episode aired. Nearly seven years later, Aaron Buerge married Angye McIntosh in August 2009. They share a daughter named Aven. “My wife Angye and our two younger daughters live in Springfield, Missouri. Our oldest daughter lives in Kansas City. This has definitely been a busy year for us!” Aaron told Us exclusively. “We just finished building our home and merged our family owned bank with Legacy Bank and Trust here in Springfield. We have been incredibly blessed. I continue to remain out of the ‘spotlight’ and continue to focus on my career and family life. I appreciate and cherish the memories I have from my days on The Bachelor. Subsequently, I have had the opportunity to take part in some things I wouldn’t have gotten to do otherwise.”.

Andrew Firestone got down on one knee during the season 3 finale of The Bachelor in 2003 and proposed to Jen Schefft. The pair split several months after the finale aired and Andrew went on to marry Ivana Bozilovic in 2008. The couple share three kids. More than a decade after his season aired, the former ABC star told Us Weekly exclusively that he’s never been happier. “All is good here. Ivana and I celebrated our 10 year wedding anniversary this past summer. Somehow she is still putting up with me! All the kiddo's are doing great, Brooks, Anja and Shane keep us busy running around to soccer/ballet/gymnastics/music/etc!” he explained. “Work is going really well and the firm I co-founded, StonePark Capital, is completing construction on our 5th hotel in San Luis Obispo, California, to open in January of 2019.” He added: “I have bit more grey hair, I work harder for my bikini body, my wife and kids started a rumor that I snore at night ... but I don't think I have been happier in my life.” In September 2025, Andrew revealed in a since-deleted post that he and Ivana split after 17 years of marriage.

In a recent development, after appearing on season 1 of The Bachelorette in 2003, Bob Guiney went to star as the fourth Bachelor later that year. While he gave Estella Gardinier a promise ring during the finale, they broke up shortly after the show aired. Months later, Bob married All My Children actress Rebecca Budig. After six years of marriage, however, the duo called it quits in 2010. He tied the knot again in November 2016 with Jessica Canyon. The couple welcomed a baby boy named Grayson in December 2018, followed by son Blake in July 2021. “I’m living in Seattle with my wife and upcoming son Grayson, who is taking up all my time these days, which I love!” Bob tells Us exclusively. “I still do ton of hosting for different live events and I go back and forth to New York twice a month to be on the Today show. I love it – they’ve very supportive of me and I love how much they make so fun of me. Life is gong very well. Thanks to the show, I’ve had such amazing opportunities come my way.”.

In a recent development, one month after the season 10 finale of The Bachelor aired in 2007, Andrew Baldwin and Tessa Horst called off their engagement but continued to see each other. Months later, the twosome split for good. And when I’m delivering their babies,” he quipped.

Chris faced legal trouble in April 2017 after he was involved in a car crash that resulted in a man’s death. In November 2018, the former Dancing With the Stars contestant pleaded guilty to a charge related to the incident. In May 2019, he was ordered to pay $2.5 million in the wrongful death lawsuit. Three months later, news broke that Chris agreed to a two-year suspended prison sentence and two years of probation. “I feel good where I’m at right now,” he told Us in December 2019. “It’s been not easy on anyone. I’m just happy that I’m able to live another day and work and do my thing and be able to do better things for the people around me.” Us broke the news in May 2020 that Chris was seeing Victoria Fuller, who competed on season 24 of The Bachelor. The twosome called it quits, however, at the end of summer 2020. “It’s complicated, but at the same time, I’m just living my life,” Victoria explained on the “Viall Files” in September 2020. “He is an amazing man and he deserves somebody super awesome who’s willing to go to Iowa and live in Iowa and right now, I’m not there yet. Maybe I will be in a couple [of] years.”.

Ben Higgins, the 20th Bachelor, got engaged to Lauren Bushnell during the 2016 finale. After The Bachelor, the pair went on to star on their own reality series titled Ben and Lauren: Happily Ever After? on Freeform for one season. In May 2017, the couple announced their split. Ben attempted to find love again during a brief stint on The Bachelor: Winter Games in 2018, but left early. Ben also cohosts a podcast called “Almost Famous” with fellow Bachelor alum Ashley Iaconetti. In February 2019, Ben revealed he had a girlfriend named Jessica Clarke. Us broke the news in March 2020 that Ben proposed to Jess in Franklin, Tennessee. They wed in November 2021 and revealed in August 2024 they were expecting their first baby. Daughter Winona arrived in February 2025. The next year, the couple shared that they are expecting their second baby. Lauren, for her part, married country singer Chris Lane in October 2019 after a year of dating. They have two sons.

Nick Viall popped the question to Vanessa Grimaldi during season 21 of The Bachelor in 2017. After several months together, the duo called it quits in August 2017. In December 2018, the reality personality, who has had a handful of acting roles in recent months, told Us exclusively that he has “no timeline” for finding a girlfriend. “It’s one of those things — you date, you see what happens,” he explained. “I still hope to meet someone someday. That could be tomorrow, that could be in five years.” After months of speculation, the "Viall Files" podcast host went public with girlfriend Natalie Joy in February 2021. In January 2023, the couple revealed that they were engaged after more than two years of dating. They welcomed daughter River Rose in February 2024 and tied the knot the following April. The couple announced in February 2026 that Natalie is pregnant with twins. Nick released a book titled Don't Text Your Ex Happy Birthday: And Other Advice on Love, Sex, and Dating in October 2022.
