Recent findings suggest that colton Underwood and Cassie Randolph briefly split during the fantasy suites episode of The Bachelor season 23, but the former NFL player sent home both Tayshia Adams and Hannah Godwin to fight for the speech pathologist’s affection. Cassie and Colton confirmed they were together during the finale. In May 2020, the couple confirmed via Instagram that they split but would remain friends. Two months later, their breakup turned messy after Cassie made an appearance on The Bachelor: The Greatest Seasons — Ever. Colton, for his part, expressed concern that she wasn’t honoring their strategy to keep their breakup private, while Cassie accused him of being hypocritical as he planned to write a upcoming chapter of his book about their split. By September 2020, the twosome were on even worse terms when Cassie filed a restraining order against Colton, accusing him of stalking and harassing her via text messages. A judge extended the restraining order to November 6, 2020, after their first hearing, but Cassie later dropped the charges. Colton came out as gay in April 2021 during an interview on Good Morning America. In February 2022, he announced his engagement to Jordan C. Brown, whom he started dating in summer 2021. The pair tied the knot in May 2023 and announced one year later that they were expecting their first baby via surrogate. Their son, Bishop Colton Brown-Underwood, was born in September 2024.

According to recent reports, the pilot’s season of the series ended with two breakups. After calling off his engagement to Hannah Ann Sluss while the show was still airing, Peter Weber revealed he still had feelings for Madison Prewett, who left the show during the finale. While Peter and Madison hoped to try to make it work, they confirmed it was over just two days after the March 2020 finale. Less than two weeks later, Peter was spotted out with another one of his contestants: Kelley Flanagan. After weeks of speculation, Us confirmed in April 2020 that the pilot and Kelley were officially in item. Two months later, they confirmed to Chris Harrison that they are planning to move to NYC together. “I remember going in, and I wanted that love story more than anything, and I can honestly say it worked out in the end,” Peter said in June 2020. “Post-show, honestly, I’m doing good. I’m extremely happy. It feels so good to be able to say that and I’m just very hopeful for the future. … I am very, very happy with this one.” Several months later, the pilot revealed in December 2020 that the couple had split. In November 2026, Peter confirmed he had married Jadeyn Carr.

The season 25 Bachelor Matt James ended his relationship with winner Rachael Kirkconnell while the show was airing in 2021 after she made headlines for her past racially insensitive actions, including resurfaced pictures of her at a party on a plantation.

While Matt previously ruled out any intends to get back together during his post-show interviews, he confirmed in May 2021 that they were officially on after being spotted together several times the month prior.

After four years of dating, Matt confirmed in January 2025 that he and Rachael had called it quits again.

Industry observers note that athlete Clayton Echard technically ended his season alone after breaking up with finalists Gabby Windey and Rachel Recchia — and later being dumped by Susie Evans, who briefly returned after her fantasy suite elimination. However, during the March 2022 finale, the Missouri native revealed that Susie reached out to him post-show. The couple aren't engaged, but they told the host that they were about to settle down in Virginia Beach. After living together for months, Clayton revealed in August 2022 that he was moving to Arizona and Susie was relocating to California. While the pair assured fans that the move wasn’t a sign of a split at the time, they called it quits that September. In September 2023, an unnamed woman claimed she was pregnant with Clayton’s babies following a one-night stand. Clayton repeatedly denied the claims. His paternity trial came to an end in June 2024, with the court siding with Clayton.

Recent findings suggest that after her relationship with Andrew Firestone ended, Jen Schefft starred as the third Bachelorette in 2005. While she selected Jerry Ferris during the finale, Jen turned down his proposal and asked him to reconsider popping the question at a later date. During the live After the Final Rose special, however, she revealed the duo had called it quits. Jen went on to marry Joe Waterman in 2009. The pair, who share daughters Mae and Charlotte, reside in Hudson, Ohio. “I grew up outside of Cleveland and my husband is from Cincinnati, so we decided to move home to be closer to family,” Jen, who is a stay-at-home mom, told Us Weekly exclusively. “People still come up to me and ask about the show quite a bit, which always surprises me!” she continued. “It's been 15 years since I was on the show, and I can't believe people still recognize me. People are always so nice and it's fun to be a small part of pop culture. … I loved my experience on the show and everything it brought into my life, but I'm a much happier person being out of the public eye. I have two daughters who keep me on my toes and a great husband. Life is good!”.

After taking three years off, The Bachelorette returned to ABC in 2008 and named DeAnna Pappas the fourth series lead. While she accepted a proposal from Jesse Csincsak during the finale and planned their wedding for May 2009, they called it quits in November 2008. Years later, DeAnna married Stephen Stagliano, whose brother competed on season 5 of The Bachelorette, in Georgia in 2012. The couple share daughter Addison and son Austin. After 11 years of marriage, DeAnna unveiled her separation from Stephen. “It is with immense sadness, Stephen & I have decided to end our relationship as a couple. We have been working hard for a long time — both as a married couple & as individuals & have come to the conclusion to remain separate,” she wrote via Instagram at the time. “We remain loving parents to our beautiful children, Addison & Austin, & will continue to raise them together with love & faith.” In 2025, Us confirmed that DeAnna was arrested after an altercation with Stephen. She was later released on bail and fired back at him in court docs of her own, denying his allegations that she had a drinking problem. DeAnna also filed a restraining order against Stephen.

In a recent development, jillian Harris and Ed Swiderski got engaged during season 5 of the ABC dating show in 2009. A year later, the twosome announced their breakup in July 2010. Jillian got engaged to her longtime boyfriend, Justin Pasutto, in 2016, and they share two kids: Leo and Annie. “It’s been almost 10 years since I’ve been on the show and so most of the PTSD is gone,” Jillian joked exclusively to Us. “It was such an incredible experience even if it wasn’t ’successful’ i wouldn’t change it for a thing. I learned so much about myself and relationships that still applies to my life today.”  “Its also hard not to connect my current career situation to the Bachelor. I had a great job prior to going on the show, but I do believe that much of life and career today would be much different if I hadn’t taken that chance. I LOVE love working on the website www.jillianharris.com, I love inspiring others, being in a position to give back to charity and also be in a career where i’m able to be super creative,” she continues. “I also was able to stick in the television industry with my role on Love it Or List it, Too, which is also a dream. Yes, I’ve worked hard and loved hard to get to where i am today both professionally and personally, but I often look back and wonder…. what If? Two beautiful children, a handsome dog, a hunky fiancé and a dream job. Is life perfect? HECK no … but I have a ton to be grateful for and i owe a slice of that to the Bachelor family and experience!”.

In a recent development, ali Fedotowsky accepted a proposal from Roberto Martinez during season 6 of The Bachelorette in 2010. After more than a year together, they declared their breakup in November 2011. Ali, now a host and Emerald Duv jewelry designer, married radio personality Kevin Manno in 2017. The couple welcomed daughter Molly in 2016 and son Riley in 2018 and live in Nashville. “I’d like to think that I would’ve met my husband regardless of the show, but the truth is if I had never gone on The Bachelor and Bachelorette, I’m not sure I would have!” Fedotowsky told Us in 2018. “I met him on another show that I wouldn’t of had the opportunity to host if I hadn’t been on the Bachelorette and now we have a daughter and a son and a beautiful life. I’m even lucky enough that I get to make a living blogging about motherhood, which I’m beyond grateful for. None of this would’ve happened the way it did if I hadn’t gone on that show. I’m beyond grateful for it!”.

Ashley Hebert and J.P. Rosenbaum got engaged during the season 7 finale of The Bachelorette in 2011. The following year, the twosome tied the knot in December 2012 and their nuptials were documented for a TV special. Ashley gave birth to their first child, a baby boy named Fordham, in September 2014. The pair welcomed their second child, a daughter named Essex, in November 2016. In August 2018, Ashley and J.P. renewed their vows during a trip to Aruba. Ashley revealed that JP was diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome, a rare neurological disorder, is a condition in which the body’s immune system attacks the nerves, in December 2019. “He is in treatment and doing well,” the pediatric dentist said at the time. “It may be a long road to full recovery, but we are so grateful to everyone that has helped us get to a speedy diagnosis and treatment.” JP, for his part, detailed his symptoms during a December hospital stay: “Things you do every day, like picking up this phone, or buttoning buttons, tying shoelaces, putting on deodorant, just can’t do it. Picking up my kids, can’t do it.” He was discharged on December 9, 2019. In October 2020, the couple announced they had split after nearly eight years of marriage. “It is with a heavy heart that I share with you that, after months of separation, Jp and I have amicably decided to go our separate ways,” Hebert captioned a photo of the couple slow-dancing on Instagram. “We created the most beautiful children and shared memories that will never be forgotten. Our differences have taken a toll on our relationship and after years of attempting to repair the damage, we’ve decided that it is in our family’s best interest to create new and separate lives for our children. Please respect our privacy as we move forward with the newness of our lives. Our ultimate focus is to create stable and healthy lives for our children. Thank you for your love and support throughout the years. Wishing you all love, happiness, and good health.” In March 2022, the dentist revealed that she has had a boyfriend for nearly one year.

Industry observers note that the Georgia-based attorney Andi Dorfman was named the 10th Bachelorette in 2014. Andi accepted a proposal from Josh Murray during the finale. While the pair moved in together in Atlanta, they confirmed their split in January 2015. Andi documented her Bachelor/Bachelorette journey in her first book, It’s Not Okay, released in 2016. She released her second book, Single State of Mind, in 2018. “Life after The Bachelorette has been a wild ride for me. People often ask if the show was good or bad for my life and without hesitation, I always say good,” Andi told Us exclusively. “I know had it not been for The Bachelorette I wouldn’t be living life in New York City and being able to say that I am an author working on my third book. And as each season goes on, I may feel a little older but feel proud and grateful to have been part of a show that has so many devoted fans and is still beloved by so many people.”  Andi added that she still speaks to “a lot of people from [her] season,” former host Harrison and a lot of fellow Bachelorettes. “Between the 13 of us, we’ve built a nice, supportive community that I didn’t expect but definitely cherish,” she explained. “Fan encounters are interesting because living in New York the vibe is less fanatic and people are too busy or in too much of a hurry to stop you, but my parents, who live in Georgia, still get people that will recognize their last name or recognize them from being on television, so I think in a funny way they are more of the stars than I am.”  In June 2020, Andi announced via Instagram that she made to move from NYC to Los Angeles. After reconnecting with an old friend named Blaine Hart in Italy during summer 2021, the pair started dating. He proposed on the beach in L.A. in March 2022. The following May, the duo tied the knot in Italy, the same place where they reconnected two years prior. On August 4, 2024, Andi shared via Instagram that she and Hart were expecting their first child, who arrived in December of that year.

Recent findings suggest that during the season 11 premiere of The Bachelorette, the men met both Kaitlyn Bristowe and fellow season 19 Bachelor contestant Britt Nilsson. The contestants then voted for Kaitlyn to be the lead for the season. During the finale, both Shawn Booth and Nick Viall got down on one knee, but Kaitlyn accepted a ring from Shawn. The pair moved to Nashville and started their lives together offscreen. Fan speculation that the couple called it quits surfaced in summer 2018, but Kaitlyn, who hosts a podcast titled “Off the Vine,” and Shawn, who opened up a gym in Nashville, did not announce the end of their engagement until November 2018. Due to the fact that the pair were together more than two years, Kaitlyn was the first woman from the franchise who got to keep her Neil Lane engagement ring after the breakup even though she did not marry Shawn. The former Bachelorette confirmed her relationship with fellow Bachelor Nation star Jason Tartick in January 2019. Months later, the duo — who exchanged “I love yous” in April 2019 — moved in together in Nashville and announced they adopted a dog. They adopted a second pup in December 2019. In June 2020, Kaitlyn confirmed that she and Jason picked out an engagement ring before she left to film season 29 of Dancing With the Stars. Almost a year later, the former banker finally popped the question during a May 2021 "Off the Vine" recording session. “It was everything I could have asked for,” Bristowe told Entertainment Tonight. “The words that came out of his mouth were insanely beautiful. We’ve never locked eyes like that in our lives. We were holding hands, so intense, and I was listening to his every word, but still blacked out.” The duo announced their split in August 2023. "Continuing our friendship is incredibly important to both of us," they wrote in a joint social media post at the time. "We feel grateful to be ending our engagement with love and respect for each other. It’s heartbreaking and sad to say goodbye, but our care and admiration for one another will never die.".

According to recent reports, joJo Fletcher accepted a proposal from Jordan Rodgers during the season 12 finale of The Bachelorette in 2012. The twosome moved to Dallas together, but as of January 2019, have no concrete wedding looks. In November 2018, JoJo, who recently launched a clothing line, told Us exclusively that she and Jordan would consider having a televised wedding. “I would never say no, never, but I think it’s very vital that, if it was a televised wedding, that it stays true and organic to us,” she explained. “We would never do a wedding that was just filled with a bunch of Bachelor people that we don’t even know, because that’s not us. But, if we could have it the exact way that we’d want it to be, and allow people to see it as well, then I would say yes.” After Jordan re-proposed in August 2019, the Cash Pad stars told Us that they plan to wed in June 2020. Their nuptials were postponed, however, amid the coronavirus pandemic. Fletcher and Rodgers finally wed in May 2022. Three years later, the couple declared they were expecting their first baby. Daughter Romy Blair arrived in December 2025.

Rachel Lindsay and Bryan Abasolo got engaged during the season 13 finale of The Bachelorette in 2017. “It’s, like, we’re either going to have this 500-plus wedding that we want, or it’s going to be super small,” Rachel said of the duo's nuptials in December 2018. “So I’m going to hurt a lot of feelings, but I’m going to have the wedding that we want, surrounded by the people we love the most and I want to do it as soon as possible. I don’t want to put off a wedding because I’m planning something big for everybody else.” The twosome ultimately tied the knot in August 2019 in Mexico. Rachel, who splits her time between Miami and Los Angeles, works for Extra and hosts the “Higher Learning” podcast with Van Lathan. In January 2022, she released a book titled Miss Me With That: Hot Takes, Helpful Tidbits, and a Few Hard Truths. Bryan filed for divorce from Rachel in January 2024 after four years of marriage and requested spousal support. Rachel said at the time that she would “eventually” share further details of the split but for the moment was “trying to take it day by day.”.

Becca Kufrin accepted a proposal from Garret Yrigoyen during the season 14 finale of The Bachelorette in 2018. The couple told Us exclusively in December 2018 that they have no plans to tie the knot yet. “No dates, no months, no venue,” she said at the time. “The only thing that we’ve talked about that we want are food trucks. I want a great taco truck and a ton of Skee-Ball machines so everyone can just play games.” In August 2019, the pair moved to San Diego together and adopted a Corgi puppy named Miss Minno. The twosome made headlines in June 2020 after Becca and Rachel recorded an emotional podcast about the Black Lives Matter movement, in which they discussed Garrett’s public support for police. “For those who are curious about my relationship with Garrett at this point, all I can say right now is I don’t know,” Becca said in June 2020." I can’t give anything more than that. It’s something that we are trying to work through and discuss and do work on at home at this time and that’s where the work will remain and that’s really the best can give you at this point.” Three months later, Becca confirmed that the pair went their separate ways. “After many conversations, we came to this decision. It wasn’t something that we just arrived at one night,” Becca explained on the “Bachelor Happy Hour” podcast. “It wasn’t based solely off of one Instagram post or somebody else’s opinions or comments. There’s much more to it. To any relationship, there’s a lot of layers, and it’s not for me to divulge details. It’s no one’s business other than what I’m telling you right now.” Becca returned to ABC for season 7 of Bachelor in Paradise and met boyfriend Thomas Jacobs. Becca proposed to Jacobs in May 2022 after less than a year of dating. Five months later, Thomas popped the question to Becca during a beach trip to Ojai, California. The duo unveiled in April 2023 that they were expecting their first child. Their baby boy was born in September 2023. One month later, the twosome said “I do” at a San Diego courthouse. Kufrin revealed in October 2025 that she and Jacobs were expecting their second baby. Their second son, Steven, was born in April 2026.

Hairstylist Clare Crawley's unprecedented season 16 journey came to an early end after she fell in love with Dale Moss when there was still 16 men remaining. During a November 2020 episode, Harrison gave Clare and Dale one-on-one time and she ultimately broke things off with the other suitors and accepted a proposal from Dale (and Tayshia Adams took over where Clare left off.) In November 2020, the pair confirmed via Instagram Live that they recently celebrated three months together and were house hunting in Sacramento, California. Their happiness was short-lived, however. Clare and Dale ended their engagement in January 2021. “We appreciate the love and support we’ve received from so many people, but this is the healthiest decision for both of us at this time,” Dale wrote via Instagram at the time. A month later, Us exclusively revealed that the twosome are back together after they were spotted holding hands in Florida. Less than one year after giving things another shot, Us confirmed in September 2021 that Clare and Dale split again. One year later, Us revealed Clare was dating a man named Ryan Dawkins. He proposed in Las Vegas in October 2022. Clare and Ryan wed in February 2023. Clare announced via Instagram in July 2023 that she and Ryan are expecting their first baby via surrogate. “Our laundry is about to get a whole lot cuter in 2024!!” she captioned a video of the couple putting a onesie on a clothesline that read, “Worth the wait.” Clare confirmed her daughter’s arrival in January 2024. “She’s here!” she wrote via Instagram, sharing a photo that revealed her hugging Ryan in a hospital room.

Season 17 star Katie Thurston got engaged to Blake Moynes during the August 2021 finale. The twosome split their time between his native Canada and her home in San Diego after filming wrapped. The Washington native unveiled in October 2021 that they called of their engagement. “It is with mutual love and respect that we have decided to go our separate ways. We are so grateful for the moments we shared together and the entire journey that has unfolded this year, but we ultimately have concluded that we are not compatible as life partners, and it is the most caring choice for both of us to move forward independently,” she wrote via Instagram at the time. “We ask for kindness and privacy as we both navigate this transition. Katie started dating comedian Jeff Arcuri in April 2024, getting engaged the following August. In February 2025, Katie revealed she was diagnosed with breast cancer. Us exclusively revealed in March 2025 that the pair tied the knot.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The second half of November is usually quiet for several reasons when it comes to latest game releases–and one other big reason–but Xbox Game Pass subscribers can look forward to several new titles to close off the month--and eight games will also be leaving Game Pass on November 30. Microsoft has revealed a handful of new additions to the Game Pass library, including a kid-friendly game to kick things off and a sneak peek at some sporty fun for the first week of December. These announcements typically come in two waves, with a sneak peek split between them, so this list isn't complete yet. The first game on the way is Paw Patrol: Dino World. Ideal for younger members of the family who definitely shouldn't be playing GTA 6 right now, this family-friendly game revolves around the PAW Patrol working together to round up lost and scared dinosaurs. Other highlights this month include Call of the Elder Gods for a Lovecraftian puzzle-adventure, High on Life 2 joining Game Pass Premium, and Roadside Research, which is all about aliens trying to run a gas station while poorly disguised as humans. If you're looking for action, Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 is worth checking out. All the thrill of long-distance sniping, with a surprising amount of close-quarters stealth gameplay as well. Also recommended is Motorslice, where you'll get to parkour through the ruins of a brutalist megastructure, climb massive bosses in tense fights, and hunt down living construction equipment. Starting in December, you can get Freestyle Football 2, which is an online multiplayer soccer game built around 5v5 matches. We already have that game in the form of Rematch from Sifu developer Sloclap, but if you want a different spin on that soccer idea, take a quick look. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem are very selective about when they work on a project together, but the opportunity to costar in director Florian Zeller's timely psychological thriller Bunker was too enticing to pass up.

In a recent development, "When [Zeller] came to us with this powerful, very necessary story to tell, we looked at each other and there was no way to say no to this," Cruz said during a post-screening discussion at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room on Sunday. "I'm very, very happy that we did it.".

Bunker revolves around a married couple, Miguel (Bardem) and Sofia (Cruz), whose 17-year marriage is tested when Miguel, a famous architect, is presented with a life changing work opportunity.

According to recent reports, “I really wanted to work with them because I truly believe they are [two] of the greatest actors working today,” Zeller said during the panel discussion moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross. “I was also very excited and interested to have them together onscreen because they are also a real couple. I thought it would be an interesting and unique opportunity to approach something that has to do with authenticity, with the truth. Not to say that this is their story, because of course this is not their story.”.

Florian Zeller at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026.

Cruz noted she felt a kinship with her character's concerns. “We have so many things in common in terms of this sadness and frustration and anger that you feel in terms of where is the world going if we don't wake up soon,” she said. “I hope it's not too late, but especially the experiment that is being done on younger people, children, teenagers, it just makes me very furious.

In a recent development, “It's something that affects me so much as an actress, as a mother, as a citizen of the world, that I felt completely a need to play Sophia,” she continued. “And of course it was not the only reason, but it was a big privilege to be able to say those lines. And [Zeller] is such a master of writing and I am a fan of all his work. And same for Javier, who is not here with us today, he's doing theater, but we are very careful in terms of choosing when to work together.”.

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026.

According to recent reports, cruz praised Zeller’s ability to provide a supportive, safe working environment and his strong point of view. “We felt really, really safe with him, he's so talented. He doesn't need any kind of manipulation and he never treats the audience as not intelligent because the audience can feel everything,” she explained. “And that has become really the most key thing for me. Don't over-explain, don't underestimate the audience ever because the thermometer is really working. And also with young people more and more and more. That is my hope to continue to go to see films on a major screen. They're coming back thank God. So let's create more possibilities so they can keep doing that.”.

Sources indicate that cruz also remarked that she and Bardem have similar approaches to their work and the preparation it requires. “It's true that we share the same passion and we have done this since we were teenagers,” she said. “We love exploring and studying and feeling that healthy fear of the unknown because every time you begin a project, in a way, it's really starting from zero. So it's a really good thing to share.”.

According to recent reports, zeller called his collaboration with the couple “a fascinating journey. It takes a lot of courage or fearlessness to do that, I think, for actors.” He also revealed that he initially referenced Stanley Kubrick's seminal thriller Eyes Wide Shut as a point of reference for Bunker, but realized it might not be setting the proper tone, given the circumstances.

Industry observers note that “I remember that the first time I spoke with [Cruz] and Javier about this project, I mentioned a film that was somewhere in my mind, Eyes Wide Shut. Not to say that there is any kind of connection between the two films, but as you remember, Eyes Wide Shut at the time, Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman, they were together," he said. "And I remember as a viewer that it was so interesting to be in a position where you do not know exactly what you're invited to watch… but Javier [later] told me, ‘You should not mention this film too often because remember at the end of the shooting they broke up.’ And then I realized that the director, Kubrick, died soon after. So I was like, ‘Okay, I'm going to stop mentioning this film.’ But the real difference I would say is that we knew that the destination of that film was the last image of the painting that you saw, which means that it was about how to reconnect with the other.”.

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026.

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

Recent findings suggest that shantel VanSanten returned to FBI as Special Agent Nina Chase in Monday’s episode, “Posterity,” which marked her second appearance on the series since FBI: Most Wanted’s cancellation in 2025. Her return came just a couple of weeks after it was revealed that Nina had been offered a job to lead her own task force in San Diego, leading Scola (John Boyd) to question the logistics of their relationship and raising their son, Dougie. As Nina continued to pack and get in one last case at 26 Fed, Scola was still wrestling with how they were going to make things work. Ultimately, he told Nina he was going to put in a transfer and follow her to San Diego, meaning another FBI exit could be looming.

As Scola pointed out, though, it will still probably be a while until the transfer goes through. However, with him eventually moving out to California and Scolina taking the FBI by storm down there, this has spinoff potential written all over it. It would be fun to follow Scola and Nina in San Diego as Nina led her own task force, but would it ever happen? VanSanten and Boyd gave their take to CinemaBlend and, hilariously, have their own opinions on the ordeal:.

Industry observers note that FBI has been growing as a franchise, like any Dick Wolf series, so it’s totally logical to wonder about a spinoff coming from this update. Having two fan-favorite characters moving across the country for the job would certainly be a missed opportunity for another series, in my humble opinion. While it sounds like there aren’t any plans, and Boyd seems to be sticking around on FBI for the time being, if VanSanten has her way, we very well could be getting a Scolina spinoff at some point in the future. While we wait and hope for that, I'm just glad that it seems like Nina is finally getting closure.

It has been revealed that as for what could happen in a potential Scolina spinoff, well, the possibilities are endless. Nina leading her own task force and seeing how she evolves in that leadership position would definitely be a great focus point. Scola would probably be settling into a newly introduced FBI field office, but the two of them would still stick to their deal of not going on cases together. We’d also probably get more of them and Dougie, who we definitely have not seen enough of. The story is there, and so are the characters, and I would love it if it happened. But if not, I’d hope that Boyd isn’t leaving FBI any time soon.

Recent findings suggest that now, for the time being, Scola will continue working out of 26 Fed. Considering all the cast changes that FBI has been through in recent years, I’m hoping that Boyd doesn’t leave the series any time soon, no matter how much I want a Scolina spinoff. Nina may be moving, but fans can still see Scola and co. in latest episodes of FBI on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming the next day on Paramount+.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, while the Breaking Bad universe would eventually expand to include dozens of characters, the pilot was actually a tidy affair.
  • According to recent reports, SHARON BIALY, casting director: I don’t know if Bryan knows this, but when Sherry [Thomas] and I went in to meet with Vince to try to get the job as casting directors—­our “audition”—­we literally mentioned, “You may think we’re crazy.
  • In a recent development, sherry and I did a lot of theater at the time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, while the Breaking Bad universe would eventually expand to include dozens of characters, the pilot was actually a tidy affair. At its center was Walter White, whose journey would require an actor of extraordinary depth and nuance. It’s not an exaggeration to say that the success or failure of Breaking Bad would rest primarily on his sagging shoulders.

According to recent reports, SHARON BIALY, casting director: I don’t know if Bryan knows this, but when Sherry [Thomas] and I went in to meet with Vince to try to get the job as casting directors—­our “audition”—­we literally mentioned, “You may think we’re crazy. We hope you don’t fire us before you hire us. But what about Bryan Cranston?” And he said, “By golly, that’s who I want. I worked with him on The X-­ Files.”.

In a recent development, sherry and I did a lot of theater at the time. We were doing Aaron Sorkin’s new play [The Farnsworth Invention], and Bryan came in and read. We were blown away. He was so talented on Malcolm in the Middle, obviously, but this was live theater with a lot of language. Anyway, Bryan didn’t get the role, but his audition was incredible. And I never forgot it.

VINCE GILLIGAN, creator: Bryan was the only guy I was thinking of when I wrote the script. I had written an episode of The X-­ Files called “Drive,” which came out in 1998, and I was lucky enough to hire him to play the bad guy.

According to recent reports, we were really struggling to cast this role because we needed a guy who could be really scary, someone who could make us feel like our hero, Agent Mulder, could get his head blown off at any second. But also, he had to be kind of an asshole. [Throughout the episode] he’s ranting about the government. He’s ranting about stuff like, “Agent Mulder— is that a Jewish name?”.

He’s a thoroughly unlikable guy. And yet you had to feel bad for him, for what happens to him at the end of the episode. You had to feel sympathy.

We only had a day or two left before production was going to start. We were going to have to settle on somebody. We had plenty of actors come in who were scary as all get out, but they weren’t necessarily likable. And then this guy walks in the door: Bryan Cranston. Never heard of him before. And he nails it in the audition. As he left, we all stood up and shook his hand, and then I looked to the other producers and to Rick Millikan, our casting director, and I stated, “Off to wardrobe!” He was that good.

When I came up with the idea of Breaking Bad, I thought, This is a guy who, again, is going to be very unlikable. He’s going to do a lot of unlikable things, and the audience still has to sympathize with him. Who would be good for this role? I know! That guy, Bryan Cranston. And I wrote it for him. I never really had anyone else in mind.

In a recent development, MELISSA BERNSTEIN, co-executive producer: He was in an episode of X-­Files, playing this racist, and somehow, over the course of the episode, you go from loathing him to feeling badly that he doesn’t make it. He just was able to make someone so unsavory be human. Vince also remarked, “And he’s so great with comedy. I just feel it in my bones that he could bring those chops to drama—­his sense of timing, the way he embodies those choices physically. He’s perfect.”.

BRYAN CRANSTON: I instruct young actors all the time that without a healthy dose of luck, you will not have a career. And this [episode of The X-­ Files] was a lucky break for me.

Recent findings suggest that I had just gotten back from shooting this little movie that I wrote and directed, called Last Chance. I spent all of our money on it, and by the end I was like, Wow, what are we doing on this film? But we rolled the dice on it, and now I was back in town and got a call from my agent about an audition. I mentioned, “Whatever it is, let me know, because I really could use the money.” It just so happened that my look at the time, from this movie that I did, was a perfect look for this guy [on The X-­Files]. So, I went in, and I got the job—­and I was grateful for it.

In a recent development, it’s only in retrospect that I realized Vince Gilligan wanted to see me [to discuss Breaking Bad] was because I had played this reprehensible character that, despite his actions, still needed the audience to root for his life. Despite the despicable person in the back seat, David Du­chovny’s humanity would not allow him to just pull over and say, “Fuck it, die. You’re a horrible human being. I just want you to die.” He couldn’t do it. That’s really, in a nutshell, what Vince Gilligan does.

I knew intuitively that coming off seven years of a comedy, I needed to look for a drama. If I didn’t, I could have been typecast. If you want to expand on the opportunities that may present themselves, you need to take control. I was offered a couple of comedy pilots that I turned down, and I was perfectly willing to wait. Then Breaking Bad came into my lap.

Sources indicate that I read it . . . and I couldn’t believe it. I was stunned. I thought, This is perhaps the best hour­-long screenplay that I’ve ever read. I felt tremendous empathy for this character. This poor guy who is just struggling. And I was the same age as Walter White—­I was fifty.

But reading the pilot, I didn’t know where it was going. You have this fish­ out­ of­ water teacher, cooking crystal meth? How could that possibly be sustained year after year after year? How can someone who knows nothing about that world survive? And Vince explained that he wanted to turn Mr. Chips into Scarface.

According to recent reports, MARK JOHNSON, executive producer: Obviously, some people came up for Walter White who were names, but we never got around to entertaining them seriously. It was Vince’s idea to cast him. And despite the fact that there wasn’t a unanimous wave of approval, there wasn’t the kind of pushback that you’d probably have today, in large part because I don’t think the expectation was that we were going to get any real name, any significant name.

Sources indicate that MELISSA BERNSTEIN: AMC had found Jon Hamm for Mad Men, and they sort of got to reintroduce him to the business. I think they thought we would do something similar with Bryan.

It has been revealed that CHARLIE COLLIER, president, general manager, AMC: I was never in the room when they were debating the cast with Vince and Mark. That would have been the programming group. And then they would come back to us and say, “They want that father from Malcolm in the Middle.” And we’d be like, “Really? He’s going to be the linchpin for this whole ambitious project?”.

CHRISTINA WAYNE, senior VP, scripted programming, AMC: When Vince suggested Bryan, we all kind of noted, “That guy from Malcolm in the Middle?” And then he started showing us a bunch of tape of Bryan in other things, and I was, like, Oh my God—­he’s a total chameleon.

Recent findings suggest that JAMIE ERLICHT, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: It’s funny. This is one of those great Hollywood stories that has been told so many times. You sit on the sidelines and watch, and it takes on a life of its own. That life is a little different than the truth, sure, but it’s a better story.

The story is that Zack [Van Amburg] and I heard “Bryan Cranston,” and we were really unsure, and we tried to convince Vince that, No, that’s not the way to go. That’s part of a story about how despite all the forces against him, Bryan Cranston became Walter White.

Sources indicate that it’s a great story. I love that story. I mean, I don’t love that story.

Sources indicate that the truth is, the show was going forward. We weren’t worried about the writing because Vince was knocking it out of the park. The directing? We weren’t worried about the directing. The casting was going to be the next critical element. If you don’t have it—­ well, it’s funny to think about it now. With ninety­ nine point nine percent of other actors in that role, that show is just a well­ written good show that doesn’t become the legacy show that it’s become. And so Vince brought up Bryan Cranston.

I had worked with Bryan on King of Queens. He was the wacky neighbor, a guest star. I was a mid­ level executive, and I was in charge of that show. I always thought he brought a lot of comedic value, just like he did on Seinfeld, and obviously Malcolm in the Middle.

So, when the name Bryan Cranston came up, I was like, Hmmm, that’s interesting. I’ve never seen him do the more dramatic stuff. Do you think he can do it?

Vince was very passionate. He said he had worked with him on X-­Files, and that’s where he really saw what he was capable of on the drama side. We said, “Great, would you send us the X-­Files episode?” Which he did. I remember it was the next day. Zack and I were watching it. We looked at each other and said, “It’s a little bit of a leap of faith, but Vince is passionate, and Bryan is truly talented. Sure, we’re in.” The process took all of thirty­ six hours.

That version of the story, the true version of the story, is not as sexy as the one where Bryan jumped through thirty­ nine hoops and almost didn’t get cast. But that’s how it happened.

In a recent development, ZACK VAN AMBURG, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: Remember, at this point, Michael Chiklis had gone from doing comedy to being a badass antihero (in The Shield). So, on one hand, you worry: Wait, are we just pulling a page out of the same playbook? Let’s take another sitcom guy and have him do a dark drama.

Recent findings suggest that I think Vince was really clear on why he wanted Bryan. There was a likability factor that was undeniable. There was also a sort of sympathy that Bryan was able to elicit. And Vince also noted, “No, wait a second—­ this guy’s also a dramatic actor.”.

While some of this stuff gets lost in the haze of time—­ and the internet has a way of transforming rumors into something disguised as fact—­ it’s fair to say that Bryan was always the first choice for the role of Walter White. Regardless of what you may have heard, no one else was offered the job. Not Matthew Broderick, not John Cusack. No one. But you can’t fault anyone for doing their due diligence.

According to recent reports, SHARON BIALY: The network likes names. They want to talk about other names. We did that. We did a couple of auditions and meetings. We just met recently with an actor on something else, and he reminded me that he was in the waiting room when Bryan walked out, and he turned to the other three actors and said, “We should all just go home. It’s over. That guy’s going to get it.”.

VINCE GILLIGAN: We saw a lot of really good actors, several of them now famous names. They never dissuaded me that Bryan was the guy. And luckily, Bryan remarked yes, because he was up at the same time for a pilot for Fox that was going to pay him . . . well, my understanding is, substantially more money. Like a doctor show. Thank goodness he went with us instead.
